Position: Senior Project Officer
Location: Dhanagdhi -5, Kailali

Youth Alliance for Development is a non-profit and non-governmental organization established in 2011 AD, propelled by a shared vision of youth empowerment. Youth Alliance for Development was founded by a dynamic cohort of young visionaries who recognize the indispensable role that the youth assume in steering the nation towards progress. YOUTH ALLIANCE FOR DEVELOPMENT (YARD) is swiftly emerging as a potent force centered on the youth, fortified by proactive measures, the promotion of youth leadership, and empowerment initiative. Serving as a catalyst for positive societal transformation, the organization serves as a crucial podium, amplifying the voices of the youth and magnifying their perspectives on matters of public importance.

Youth Alliance for Development (YARD) is implementing the Women Empowerment and Child Rights Protection (WECP) Projects in Godawari Municipality of Kailali District in partnership with Kindernothilfe Nepal (KNH). And coordination with local and provincial governments as well as other stakeholders. Therefore, YARD invites applications from interested qualified and professional Nepali candidates for the following full-time positions.

Position Description: The Senior Project Officer will be responsible for the overall planning, implementation, coordination, monitoring, and reporting of assigned projects at the field level. The position will provide overall project leadership and ensure that project activities are implemented effectively, efficiently, and in accordance with approved project plans, organizational policies, donor requirements, and government regulations.

Reports to: Program Manager

Duty station: Project Office Dhangadhi Kailali and frequently field visit at project implementation location.

Major responsibilities:

1. Project Planning and Implementation

  • Lead and coordinate the overall implementation of project activities at the field level.
  • Prepare and implement detailed project work plans, activity schedules, and implementation strategies.
  • Ensure that project activities are delivered on time, within the approved budget, and according to required quality standards.
  • Coordinate with project teams, partners, community groups, and stakeholders for effective implementation.
  • Identify implementation challenges and recommend timely and practical solutions.
  • Ensure that project activities are aligned with approved proposals, log frames, budgets, and organizational priorities.

2. Coordination with Government and Stakeholders

  • Establish and maintain effective coordination with local government authorities and relevant government agencies.
  • Represent the organization/project in meetings, workshops, coordination forums, and other relevant platforms as delegated.
  • Maintain strong relationships with community leaders, beneficiaries, partners, and other stakeholders.
  • Facilitate regular communication and coordination among project stakeholders.
  • Ensure that project activities comply with relevant government policies, regulations, and local requirements.

3. Financial Management and Compliance

  • Support effective management of project funds in accordance with approved budgets and organizational financial procedures.
  • Prepare and process payment requests, advances, settlements, and other project-related financial documentation.
  • Ensure proper documentation and verification of payments and disbursements.
  • Monitor project expenditures against approved budgets and identify variances or potential financial risks.
  • Conduct basic financial analysis and provide recommendations to improve budget utilization and cost effectiveness.
  • Ensure compliance with organizational financial policies, donor financial requirements, and applicable government regulations.
  • Maintain complete and accurate financial and supporting documentation for audit and reporting purposes.
  • Coordinate with the Finance Department to ensure timely financial reporting and settlement of advances.

4. Monitoring, Reporting and Documentation

  • Monitor project progress against approved objectives, indicators, targets, and work plans.
  • Prepare regular project progress reports, field reports, and other required reports.
  • Contribute to donor, management, and government reports as required.
  • Maintain accurate project records, databases, attendance sheets, activity reports, photographs, and other supporting documents.
  • Track project outputs, outcomes, achievements, challenges, and lessons learned.
  • Support data collection, analysis, verification, and documentation of project results.

5. Team Leadership and Supervision

  • Provide technical and operational guidance to project staff and field teams.
  • Supervise, mentor, and support project staff to ensure effective performance.
  • Organize regular team meetings and review progress against agreed work plans.
  • Promote teamwork, accountability, professionalism, and a results-oriented working environment.
  • Identify staff capacity-building needs and support relevant training and coaching.

6. Quality Assurance and Risk Management

  • Ensure that project activities meet organizational and donor quality standards.
  • Identify operational, financial, programmatic, and compliance risks and recommend mitigation measures.
  • Ensure adherence to organizational policies, safeguarding standards, code of conduct, and relevant procedures.
  • Support internal and external audits by providing required project and financial documentation.
  • Ensure corrective actions from monitoring visits, audits, and reviews are properly followed up.

7. Communication and Knowledge Management

  • Maintain regular communication with management regarding project progress, challenges, risks, and achievements.
  • Document good practices, lessons learned, success stories, and case studies.
  • Share relevant project information with internal and external stakeholders as appropriate.
  • Contribute to organizational learning and improvement of project implementation practices.

8. Key Deliverables

  • Timely and quality implementation of project activities.
  • Achievement of project targets and indicators.
  • Effective coordination with local government and project stakeholders.
  • Accurate and timely project and financial reporting.
  • Proper payment, disbursement, and financial documentation.
  • Effective budget monitoring and utilization.
  • Complete project documentation and audit-ready records.
  • Timely identification and resolution of project implementation issues.

Competencies:

Academic Qualification and Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Project Management, Development Studies, Social Sciences, Sociology, and Rural development. A Master’s degree will be an advantage.
  • Minimum 5 years of relevant experience in project/program management, preferably within an NGO, INGO, development organization, or donor-funded project.
  • Demonstrated experience in field-level project implementation and coordination.
  • Experience working with local government authorities and community stakeholders.
  • Experience in project budgeting, financial monitoring, payment/disbursement processes, and compliance.
  • Experience in preparing project progress and financial reports.
  • Good understanding of donor compliance and government requirements.
  • Experience supervising and coordinating project teams.

Required Skills and Competencies

  • Strong project planning and management skills.
  • Excellent coordination and stakeholder management skills.
  • Good financial management and analytical skills.
  • Strong report writing and documentation skills.
  • Good knowledge of MS Office, particularly Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
  • Strong communication, negotiation, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities.
  • Strong leadership and team management skills.
  • High level of integrity, accountability, and attention to detail.
  • Ability and willingness to travel frequently to project field locations.

A. Child and adult safeguarding and sponsorship business

  • Manage all the working environment in the office and working areas are child and adult sensitive
  • Guide the team and organization in managing protection related matters appropriately
  • Support the organization in complying with all children and adult safeguarding policies, requirements and audits
  • Manage all the businesses as per the protocols and guidance provided by KNH
  • Children participation is well reflected in the reporting platforms provided.

For details

Interested candidates are requested to submit their application along with an updated CV and cover letter and other required related documents (Citizenship, educational related documents, experience related documents and other) as well as two references by 31 August 2026 before 5 PM, via email at yard.vacancy2025@gmail.com. Or visit to www.yard.org.np and send the CV. Organization cannot select those who have not fulfil the required criteria of education, not received them in time. Organization has policy and practice on Protection of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSEAH), child protection policy, Complaint and Feedback Response Mechanism Management Policy and Anti-corruption, fraud, bribery and dishonesty. Organization would like to request to declare near relationship of any person related to organization with candidates and or any conflict of interest. Position: Provincial Coordinator
Project: Reclaiming Advocacy through Narratives, Debates, Grassroot Theatre and Arts (RANGA)
Organization: Debate Network Nepal (DNN)
Duty Station: Surkhet
Reports To: National Program Coordinator
Contract Duration: Until 31 December 2028 (with 3-month probation period)
Application Deadline: 05 September 2026

1. Background

The project Reclaiming Advocacy through Narratives, Debates, Grassroot Theatre and Arts (RANGA) aims to promote youth engagement in Nepal through culture and creativity. Using art and cultural tools such as theatre, debate, storytelling, and digital media, the project empowers youth as creators, advocates, and professionals, enabling them to actively contribute to civic life and community development.

The project mobilizes youth-led NGOs and community groups across provinces of Nepal, strengthening their capacity to lead inclusive cultural initiatives. It integrates cross-cutting priorities including gender equality, social inclusion, and the “leave no one behind” principle, with particular focus on marginalized youth including Dalit, Indigenous communities, persons with disabilities, gender-diverse individuals, and LGBTIQ+ communities, especially intersex individuals.

RANGA is implemented in consortium partnership with Mandala Theatre Nepal (Lead Partner) and Campaign for Change, with Debate Network Nepal (DNN) serving as a key implementing partner responsible for debate, dialogue, and youth engagement components.
The project is expected to run until December 2028.

2. Purpose of the Position

The Provincial Coordinator will be responsible for coordinating and implementing RANGA Project activities at the provincial level and supporting Debate Network Nepal’s wider provincial engagement, in alignment with approved work plans, budgets, organizational priorities, and donor requirements.

The position will support provincial-level financial planning and budgeting processes, including the timely tracking of expenses, collection of supporting documents, and compliance with project, organizational, and donor requirements.

The Provincial Coordinator will work closely with the National Program Coordinator, the Kathmandu-based DNN team, consortium partners, local governments, educational institutions,
youth networks, and other relevant stakeholders to ensure effective implementation, reporting, visibility, and stakeholder engagement.

3. Key Responsibilities

3.1 Program Implementation

  • Coordinate and implement project activities at the provincial level including workshops, debates, theatre engagements, fellowships, advocacy events, and trainings.
  • Ensure inclusive participation of marginalized youth groups.
  •  Identify and mobilize local youth groups, artists, facilitators, and stakeholders.
  •  Ensure activities are delivered according to approved plans and timelines.

3.2 DNN Provincial Engagement and Organizational Support

  •  Support the planning, coordination, and implementation of DNN’s provincial activities beyond the RANGA Project, as assigned by the National Program Coordinator or DNN management.
  • Strengthen DNN’s visibility, presence, and relationships with debate clubs, youth networks, educational institutions, local governments, civil-society organizations, and other relevant stakeholders in the province.
  •  Facilitate and support provincial debate clubs, youth learning spaces, dialogue sessions, trainings, competitions, and other DNN-led youth engagement initiatives.
  •  Identify opportunities for collaboration, partnerships, local resource mobilization, and expansion of DNN’s programs within the province.
  •  Collect and share provincial-level opportunities, emerging youth issues, stakeholder feedback, and relevant information that can inform DNN’s programme development, advocacy, and future proposals.
  •  Support communication and visibility of DNN’s provincial activities by collecting stories, photographs, participant testimonials, and activity updates, in line with DNN’s communication and safeguarding policies.
  •  Represent DNN in relevant provincial and local meetings, networks, and events, when assigned.

3.3 Financial and Budget Support

  •  Support preparation of provincial activity budgets in coordination with the National Program Coordinator and Admin, Finance and Documentation Officer.
  •  Track provincial-level expenditures and ensure alignment with approved budgets.
  • Maintain proper documentation of financial records and submit supporting documents in a timely manner.
  • Support financial compliance in accordance with donor and organizational policies.

3.4 Coordination and Government Liaison

  •  Coordinate with local governments and relevant provincial and municipal authorities for program implementation and collaboration.
  •  Maintain regular communication with consortium partners for smooth provincial implementation.
  •  Build and maintain relationships with local stakeholders, youth networks, and cultural institutions.
  •  Represent DNN in provincial-level and local-level coordination meetings when required.

3.5 Documentation, Communication, and Reporting

  •  Maintain systematic documentation of provincial activities including attendance sheets, reports, photographs, and case studies.
  •  Prepare and submit timely activity reports and updates to the Kathmandu office.
  • Support communication-related work including collection of stories, testimonials, and visibility materials.
  •  Provide inputs for consolidated technical and narrative reporting.

3.6 Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E)

  • Collect and maintain beneficiary data in line with project indicators.
  •  Ensure disaggregated data collection (gender, inclusion categories, province).
  •  Support monitoring visits and review meetings.
  •  Provide evidence-based documentation of provincial-level impact.

3.7 Compliance and Safeguarding

  •  Ensure adherence to donor regulations and DNN’s internal policies.
  •  Promote inclusion, non-discrimination, safeguarding, and PSEA principles.
  •  Maintain confidentiality and ethical standards in working with beneficiaries and stakeholders.

4. Deliverables

  • Timely implementation of provincial-level activities.
  •  Monthly progress updates to the National Program Coordinator.
  •  Properly documented financial and narrative activity files.
  •  Updated beneficiary tracking data.
  •  Inputs to interim and final reports.

5. Duration and Contract Conditions

  •  Contract valid until 31 December 2028, subject to satisfactory performance and project continuity.
  •  Initial probation period of 3 months.
  • The position is based in Surkhet, Karnali Province.
  • Occasional travel required within the province and, when necessary, outside the province to Kathmandu or other provinces for project-related activities.

6. Reporting and Supervision

The Provincial Coordinator will report directly to the National Program Coordinator and will coordinate closely with:

  • Managing Director and, Admin, Finance and Documentation Officer (Kathmandu office)
  • Consortium partners
  •  Local governments and relevant authorities
  •  Provincial stakeholders and youth networks

7. Required Qualifications and Experience

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in Social Sciences, Development Studies, Management, Arts, Humanities, or related field.

Experience

  •  Minimum 1–2 years of relevant experience in project implementation, youth engagement, community mobilization, or cultural initiatives.
  •  Experience working with NGOs or donor-funded projects preferred.

Skills and Competencies

  •  Strong coordination and facilitation skills.
  • Basic budgeting and financial tracking skills.
  •  Good communication skills in Nepali and English.
  •  Ability to work independently at provincial level.
  •  Strong documentation and reporting skills.
  •  Commitment to inclusion, diversity, and youth empowerment.

8. Application Deadline: 03 September 2026

9. How to Apply

Interested and qualified candidates are requested to submit the following documents:

  • A cover letter explaining their interest in the position and suitability for the role
  • An updated CV, including contact details of at least two professional references
  •  Copies of relevant academic certificates and citizenship/identity document

Applications should be sent by email to debate.dnn@gmail.com with the subject line:

Application for Provincial Coordinator – Surkhet

9. Ethical Standards

The position holder must adhere to:

  • DNN’s Code of Conduct.
  •  Anti-discrimination and inclusion principles.
  • Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA).
  •  Transparency and accountability standards.
  •  Confidentiality requirements.

Reporting & Market Intelligence

  • Maintain accurate documentation related to partners, agents, branding activities, and field operations.
  • Provide actionable market insights and recommendations to support strategic decision-making.

Required Skills

  • Solid understanding of local market dynamics, customer behavior, and partner ecosystems.

Youth Innovation Lab (YI-Lab) is a not-for-profit civic tech company that works at the intersection of emerging cutting-edge technological tools and their applications by equipping young professionals to solve emerging challenges in our community. YI-Lab’s mission statement is, ‘to engage young people to bridge science to people and policy through innovation’. YI-Lab harnesses indigenous knowledge, citizen science approach, develops low-cost technological solutions, promotes open data, promotes entrepreneurship, and conducts evidence-based advocacy campaigns. YI-Lab provides a conducive environment for young people to co-create solutions for inclusive development.

Position Overview

The Program Coordinator will support the effective planning, coordination, implementation, monitoring, and reporting of programs and projects undertaken by Youth Innovation Lab. The position will work closely with program teams, partners, consultants, trainers, participants, government and non-government stakeholders, and support departments to ensure activities are delivered on time, within scope, and in accordance with organizational and donor requirements.

The Program Coordinator will play a key role in translating project plans into well-coordinated activities while maintaining strong documentation, stakeholder communication, program quality, and learning.

Key Responsibilities

Program Planning and Implementation

  • Coordinate day-to-day implementation of assigned projects and program activities.
  • Prepare and regularly update work plans, activity schedules, timelines, and implementation trackers.
  • Coordinate workshops, trainings, consultations, meetings, campaigns, field activities, and other project events.
  • Ensure activities are implemented according to approved project documents, timelines, and expected results.
  • Identify implementation challenges and coordinate timely solutions with the Program Manager/Project Lead.

Stakeholder and Partner Coordination

  • Maintain regular coordination with project partners, consultants, trainers, participants, institutions, and relevant stakeholders.
  • Support communication and follow-up with government agencies, development partners, civil society organizations, academic institutions, private-sector actors, and youth networks as required.
  • Organize coordination meetings and document key decisions, responsibilities, and follow-up actions.

Training and Event Coordination

  • Coordinate logistical and programmatic arrangements for trainings, bootcamps, workshops, conferences, and other events.
  • Support trainers and facilitators with participant information, training materials, schedules, venues, and required resources.
  • Support participant recruitment, registration, communication, attendance, and post-event follow-up.
  • Ensure training and event documentation is properly maintained.

Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning

  • Support the collection and maintenance of project data, participant information, activity outputs, and performance indicators.
  • Monitor implementation progress against approved work plans and project targets.
  • Coordinate participant feedback, pre/post assessments, surveys, and other monitoring tools.
  • Document lessons learned, success stories, challenges, and good practices.
  • Work with relevant team members to use monitoring findings for continuous program improvement.

Reporting and Documentation

  • Prepare activity reports, meeting minutes, progress updates, participant records, and other project documentation.
  • Contribute to periodic narrative and donor reports.
  • Maintain organized digital and physical project records.
  • Ensure supporting documentation is complete and available for monitoring, reporting, auditing, and institutional learning.

Budget, Procurement and Administration Coordination

  • Coordinate with the Finance and Administration team on activity budgets, procurement requests, payments, travel, logistics, and supporting documentation.
  • Monitor activity-level expenditures in coordination with relevant team members.
  • Ensure program activities follow organizational procedures and donor requirements.

Communications and Outreach

  • Coordinate with the communications team to support project visibility, outreach, participant engagement, and dissemination.
  • Provide accurate program information, activity highlights, participant stories, and results for communication materials.
  • Support outreach to relevant institutions, networks, communities, and target beneficiaries.

GESI, Safeguarding and Compliance

  • Promote gender equality, social inclusion, accessibility, and meaningful participation of underrepresented groups across program activities.
  • Ensure project implementation follows organizational safeguarding, ethical, and data protection standards.
  • Support compliance with donor requirements, organizational policies, and relevant laws and regulations.

Required Qualifications and Experience

  • Minimum Bachelor’s degree in Development Studies, Management, Social Sciences, Public Administration, International Relations, Business Administration, Project Management, or another relevant discipline.
  • Preferably 3–5 years of relevant professional experience in program/project coordination, development programs, youth engagement, innovation, education, technology, governance, or related sectors.
  • Experience coordinating donor-funded or multi-stakeholder projects is preferred.
  • Experience organizing trainings, workshops, events, or capacity-building activities.
  • Experience in project documentation, monitoring, reporting, and stakeholder coordination.

Required Skills and Competencies

  • Strong program and project coordination skills.
  • Excellent organizational and time-management skills.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills in English and Nepali.
  • Ability to manage multiple activities and deadlines simultaneously.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and interpersonal skills.
  • Good report writing and documentation skills.
  • Working knowledge of monitoring, evaluation, and results tracking.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, and digital collaboration tools.
  • Ability to work collaboratively in multidisciplinary and multicultural teams.
  • Strong problem-solving, adaptability, and attention to detail.
  • Willingness to travel to project implementation areas when required.

Key Working Relationships

The Program Coordinator will work closely with:

  • Executive Director and Program Leadership
  • Project/Program Managers and Program Team
  • Finance and Administration Team
  • Communications Team
  • Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Team
  • Consultants, trainers, mentors, and technical experts
  • Partner organizations and consortium members
  • Government agencies, development partners, academic institutions, civil society organizations, private-sector actors, and participating communities

Performance Expectations

Performance will be assessed based on timely and quality implementation of assigned activities, achievement of project deliverables, stakeholder coordination, quality of documentation and reporting, compliance with organizational and donor requirements, effective teamwork, and contribution to overall program outcomes.

Equal Opportunity

Youth Innovation Lab is committed to equal opportunity, inclusion, and non-discrimination. All staff members are expected to uphold organizational values, safeguarding standards, professional ethics, and respectful workplace practices.

We are committed to promoting workforce diversity and strongly encourage applications from youth and young professionals, especially those who identify as women, members of indigenous communities, and minority caste groups.

Interviews will be conducted on a rolling basis. Therefore, we encourage interested candidates to apply at their earliest convenience. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for an interview.
! Due to the large number of applications received, we are unable to contact each applicant individually regarding the status of their application. Please be advised that if you do not receive any email, call, or contact from Youth Innovation Lab within three weeks from the date of the application deadline, you may consider yourself as not being selected for the position at this time.  

Deadline for submission of application: 28 August 2026

title.rendered: Training and Education Manager/Consultant, Outreach Manager/Consultant

content.rendered:
Child Workers in Nepal Concerned Centre (CWIN-Nepal) is a leading child rights organization dedicated to promoting the protection, wellbeing, and development of children and adolescents across Nepal. Through its Outreach and Research Centre, CWIN-Nepal works to strengthen Child and Adolescent Mental Health (CAMH) services by increasing awareness, building the capacity of service providers, and enhancing access to quality mental health care for children, adolescents, and their families.

CWIN-Nepal is also actively engaged in child and adolescent mental health research to generate evidence that informs policies, programs, and service delivery systems. The organization collaborates with national and international partners to conduct research, develop innovative interventions, and promote evidence-based practices that contribute to the prevention, early identification, and management of mental health problems among children and adolescents.

To support these efforts, CWIN-Nepal invites applications from qualified and experienced candidates for the position of:

Training and Education Manager/Consultant and, ii) Outreach Manager/ Consultant.

Position Title: Training and Education Manager/Consultant

Number of Positions: 1

Duty Station: Outreach and Research Centre, CWIN-Nepal with possibility of 5-6 days of field work within or out of Kathmandu valley per month.

Job Purpose

The Training and Education Manager/Consultant is responsible for designing, implementing, and overseeing training and educational programs on CAMH to build the capacity of target groups such as health workers, community workers, and other stakeholders. The role ensures high-quality learning experiences aligned with CWIN’s mission.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design and develop structured training curricula, modules, and learning materials on CAMH.
  • Identify training needs on CAMH through assessments, field feedback, and stakeholder consultations.
  • Integrate evidence-based approaches and contextual relevance into training content.
  • Plan and conduct training sessions, workshops, and capacity-building activities on CAMH.
  • Coordinate and manage trainers, facilitators, and subject experts.
  • Ensure participatory, inclusive, and learner-centered training methodologies.
  • Develop long-term training and education strategies on CAMH aligned with CWIN’s objectives.
  • Expand training programs across sectors (e.g., health, education, community).
  • Promote innovative learning approaches.
  • Develop tools to assess training effectiveness and participant learning outcomes.
  • Monitor training quality and impact through feedback, assessments, and follow-up.
  • Use data to refine and improve training programs.
  • Collaborate with institutions, government bodies, and partners for training initiatives.
  • Build networks with trainers, academic institutions, and technical experts.
  • Conduct regular field visit for outreach activities, monitoring and supervision.
  • Represent the CWIN in training-related forums and events.
  • Develop and update training manuals, guidelines, toolkits, and IEC materials on CAMH.
  • Ensure materials are culturally appropriate and accessible to diverse audiences.
  • Maintain a repository of training resources and best practices.
  • Develop and write grant proposals to secure findings for the outreach center.

Required Qualifications and Experience

  • MD in Psychiatry from a recognized institution / MPhil in Clinical Psychology.
  • Mandatory registration with the Nepal Medical Council (NMC) / Nepal Health Professional Council (NHPC), as applicable.
  • Demonstrated experience in child and adolescent mental health, community outreach, training, stakeholder engagement, and capacity-building initiatives.
  • Experience in conducting, managing, or supporting mental health research projects will be an added advantage.
  • Strong communication, facilitation, report-writing, and teamwork skills.
  • Ability to work effectively with government agencies, educational institutions, health facilities, community organizations, and development partners.
  • Experience in program monitoring, evaluation, documentation, and reporting.

Position Title: Outreach Manager/Consultant

Number of Positions: 1

Duty Station: Outreach and Research Centre, CWIN-Nepal with possibility of 5-6 days of field work within or out of Kathmandu valley per month.

Job Purpose

The Outreach Manager/Consultant leads the design, implementation, and evaluation of outreach initiatives that promote mental health awareness and prevent child and adolescent mental health (CAMH) problems in schools and communities. The role focuses on strengthening stakeholder engagement, building local capacity, and ensuring programs are evidence-based and aligned with CWIN’s mission.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and implement outreach strategies to increase the visibility and impact of CWIN’s CAMH programs.
  • Build and maintain partnerships with key stakeholders, including government agencies, NGOs, schools, and community leaders.
  • Deliver CAMH orientation sessions for diverse stakeholder groups.
  • Provides / facilitate training on empathy, resilience, and psychosocial support for those working with vulnerable children.
  • Conduct regular field visit for outreach activities, monitoring and supervision.
  • Design and disseminate culturally appropriate child and adolescents mental health awareness materials (e.g., brochures, IEC resources) for schools, community health centers, and hospitals.
  • Plan, implement, and evaluate research-based outreach programs for children, adolescents, caregivers, and service providers.
  • Lead teachers training on child violence, psychosocial support, and early identification of emotional and behavioral difficulties.
  • Implement and assess Social and Emotional Learning (SEL) programs for teachers and school nurses, focusing on communication, empathy, trauma-informed care, and child-friendly practices.
  • Organize and deliver capacity-building training in CAMH for community workers (e.g., FCHVs, social mobilizers, and outreach staff).
  • Establish and strengthen referral pathways for children with severe mental health needs, linking community services with specialized care.
  • Support the development of teleconsultation services to expand access to mental health care in remote areas.
  • Conduct follow-up visits, mentoring, and supportive supervision to ensure quality implementation and skill retention.
  • Monitor, document, and report on the outcomes and impact of outreach activities.
  • Coordinate with schools, health facilities, and community structures to expand coverage and ensure sustainability.
  • Develop and write grant proposals to secure findings for the outreach center.

Required Qualifications and Experience

  • MD in Psychiatry from a recognized institution / MPhil in Clinical Psychology.
  • Mandatory registration with the Nepal Medical Council (NMC) /Nepal Health Professional Council (NHPC), as applicable.
  • Demonstrated experience in child and adolescent mental health, community outreach, training, stakeholder engagement, and capacity-building initiatives.
  • Experience in conducting, managing, or supporting mental health research projects will be an added advantage.
  • Strong communication, facilitation, report-writing, and teamwork skills.
  • Ability to work effectively with government agencies, educational institutions, health facilities, community organizations, and development partners.
  • Experience in program monitoring, evaluation, documentation, and reporting.

Application Process

Interested and qualified candidates are requested to submit:

  • An updated Curriculum Vitae (CV)
  • A cover letter highlighting their suitability for the position

Applications should be sent to vacancy.cwinnepal@gmail.com no later than 3 September 2026.

Established in 2009, YUWA is a registered not-for-profit, purely youth-run and led organization that promotes youth participation through empowerment and advocacy. YUWA was born out of a group of committed youths, unofficially working in this sector since 2005. The initial focus was to develop the leadership skills of the youths involved, to train as youth activists, and to advocate for change, thus resulting in a wide and diverse array of knowledge, skills, and experience in this sector. It led to the realization of the seriousness of youth issues and the need to act, which finally took the shape of YUWA.

YUWA currently works in three thematic areas: Active Citizenship, Sexual and Reproductive Rights and Research Unit

Department: Communication, Documentation, and Learning Department

The Communication, Documentation, and Learning Department at YUWA is a cornerstone of the organization’s mission to enhance communication, document project activities, and foster a culture of continuous learning. This department plays a crucial role in shaping the narrative of YUWA’s impactful work, ensuring effective documentation of projects, and facilitating knowledge sharing within the organization.

The Communication, Documentation, and Learning Department is dedicated to facilitating transparent and impactful communication both internally and externally. It oversees the development and implementation of communication strategies, the meticulous documentation of project activities, and the promotion of a learning culture across YUWA. It collaborates closely with internal stakeholders, including program officers, the creative department, and other relevant teams within the organization. Additionally, the department engages with external stakeholders such as donors, partners, and policymakers to enhance YUWA’s visibility and reputation.

Position Title: Communication, Documentation, and Learning Assistant

Job Responsibilities:

Communication Strategy:

  • Maintain YUWA’s social media content calendar and digital content creation across all YUWA platforms.
  • Assist in formulating and executing internal and external communication strategies.
  • Collaborate work within the communication department to evolve goal-oriented communication plans.
  • Ensure learning outcomes are thoughtfully included in new programs and strategically disseminated.
  • Cultivate creative strategies to engage YUWA’s target beneficiaries effectively.
  • Help YUWA in integrating knowledge, learning management, and preserving institutional memory into their every project, activity, report and strategy.
  • Build and sustain relationships with donors in accordance with YUWA’s partnership values.
  • Conduct frequent meetings with the team members as specified in the project details, document and disseminate the meeting learnings.

Social Media Responsibilities:

  • Develop visually striking designs for social media posts that strictly adhere to YUWA’s branding guidelines.
  • Collaborate with team members to gather images, logos, stats, and content for infographics and social media posts.
  • Support in Design, Dissemination and Integration of Quizzes, Evidence Generation survey-sheets, and Social Media Engagement Plans as part of, and to inform program activities.
  • Implement analytics and reporting mechanisms to measure the effectiveness of social media efforts.

Branding and Design:

  • Ensure that all publications, annual reports, research, reports, and products strictly adhere to the established branding guidelines.
  • Innovate and create ideas for print, electronic, web-based, and animated presentations.
  • Produce creative audio-visual materials for social media and websites, showcasing proficiency in video editing and animation.
  • Design reports and communication materials for both print and electronic distribution, incorporating a diverse range of formats such as banners, posters, booklets, leaflets, calendars, bulletins, and flyers.
  • Develop customizable templates for various purposes, including presentations and business cards, using industry-standard design tools (e.g., Adobe Creative Suite, Canva).
  • Conduct a meticulous review of final visual designs, ensuring accuracy and strict adherence to YUWA’s branding guidelines.
  • Coordinate with team members to collect images, logos, statistics, and content for infographics and social media posts.
  • Attend meetings and be engaged in content which will increase positive PR of YUWA in accordance with YUWA values, mission and vision.
  • Undertake photography and videography responsibilities at all official YUWA events, maintaining a consistent visual style aligned with the organization’s brand.

Additional Tasks:

  • Execute tasks delegated by the supervisor or management, ensuring prompt and effective completion.
  • Perform any other duties as assigned relevant to the scope of the role.
  • Contribute to and participate in organization-wide tasks, such as staff meetings, staff capacity development activities, annual retreat, evaluation and planning meetings, staff representation at Annual General Meetings, intern/volunteer/visitor orientation, and others.

Minimum Qualifications and Transferable Skills

  • Bachelor’s degree (ongoing or completed) in media studies, mass communication, journalism, gender studies, social work, and other relevant subjects with excellent command of Photoshop, Illustrator, Adobe Premiere, and video editing tools.
  • Proven skills in photography and videography, and technical operations related to communications.
  • Proficiency in multimedia format and ability to align with overall branding guidelines.
  • At least one year of internship experience in graphic design, content creation, and creative field is preferred although freshers are encouraged to apply. Proficiency in designing software tools, including graphic design software (e.g., Adobe Creative Suite, InDesign) and video editing software, is expected
  • Background or experience in creative storytelling or strategic communication is a plus.

Reporting Lines

The Communication, Documentation, and Learning Assistant will report to the members of the Executive Board who will oversee the communication department.

Working Relationships

The Communication, Documentation, and Learning Assistant will establish and maintain effective working relationships with the program department and work in coordination with program coordinators and other team members.

International Nepal Fellowship (Nepal) is a Non-Government Organization established in 1952 and serves the poor and disadvantaged people of Nepal to enable life to its fullness through health and development services. INF Nepal is currently working in health and community development services in the Gandaki, Lumbini, Karnali, and Sudurpashchim Provinces of Nepal.

For the following positions, INF Nepal is seeking competent, skilled, service oriented, and devoted Nepali citizens who shares our vision, mission, and values.

Location: Green Pastures Hospital, Pokhara

Purpose of the Job:

The post holder serves as the operational leader, ensuring that clinical, rehabilitation, financial, administrative, and community services function efficiently while supporting the organization’s mission and sustainability. The post-holder needs to be able to recognize where change is needed and implement accordingly to ensure processes are efficient and up to date, identify issues and bottlenecks early, develop appropriate plans to address them, and focus on achieving required outcomes rather than simply maintaining the status quo.

Position: Medical Officer

The role focuses on initial patient assessment, stabilization, ongoing clinical management, accurate documentation, and performance of essential procedures within competency, effective communication with consultants and multidisciplinary teams, and participation in shift-based service delivery.

Women Forum for Women in Nepal (WOFOWON), established in 2008 (2064 B.S.), is Nepal’s first worker-led, non-profit organization advocating for the rights of women workers in the informal, entertainment, and hospitality sectors, including dance bars, dohori venues, spa/massage parlors, cabin restaurants, and local eateries.

With a feminist approach, WOFOWON organizes women workers, amplifies their collective voices, and strengthens the feminist labor movement to promote their human and labor rights.

To strengthen our initiatives and advance our campaign for social justice and labor rights, WOFOWON invites applications from dedicated and qualified professionals for the following position(s):

Position: Admin & Finance Officer

Key Responsibilities

  • Manage day-to-day accounting, financial records, petty cash and bank transactions.

  • Support payroll, procurement, logistics and general office administration.

About the organization

Youth Innovation Lab (YI-Lab) is a not-for-profit civic tech company that works at the intersection of emerging cutting-edge technological tools and their applications by equipping young professionals to solve emerging challenges in our community. YI-Lab’s mission statement is, ‘to engage young people to bridge science to people and policy through innovation’. YI-Lab harnesses indigenous knowledge, citizen science approach, develops low-cost technological solutions, promotes open data, promotes entrepreneurship, and conducts evidence-based advocacy campaigns. YI-Lab provides a conducive environment for young people to co-create solutions for inclusive development.

Position Overview

The Program Coordinator will support the effective planning, coordination, implementation, monitoring, and reporting of programs and projects undertaken by Youth Innovation Lab. The position will work closely with program teams, partners, consultants, trainers, participants, government and non-government stakeholders, and support departments to ensure activities are delivered on time, within scope, and in accordance with organizational and donor requirements.

The Program Coordinator will play a key role in translating project plans into well-coordinated activities while maintaining strong documentation, stakeholder communication, program quality, and learning.

Key Responsibilities

Program Planning and Implementation

  • Coordinate day-to-day implementation of assigned projects and program activities.
  • Prepare and regularly update work plans, activity schedules, timelines, and implementation trackers.
  • Coordinate workshops, trainings, consultations, meetings, campaigns, field activities, and other project events.
  • Ensure activities are implemented according to approved project documents, timelines, and expected results.
  • Identify implementation challenges and coordinate timely solutions with the Program Manager/Project Lead.

Stakeholder and Partner Coordination

  • Maintain regular coordination with project partners, consultants, trainers, participants, institutions, and relevant stakeholders.
  • Support communication and follow-up with government agencies, development partners, civil society organizations, academic institutions, private-sector actors, and youth networks as required.
  • Organize coordination meetings and document key decisions, responsibilities, and follow-up actions.

Training and Event Coordination

  • Coordinate logistical and programmatic arrangements for trainings, bootcamps, workshops, conferences, and other events.
  • Support trainers and facilitators with participant information, training materials, schedules, venues, and required resources.
  • Support participant recruitment, registration, communication, attendance, and post-event follow-up.
  • Ensure training and event documentation is properly maintained.

Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning

  • Support the collection and maintenance of project data, participant information, activity outputs, and performance indicators.
  • Monitor implementation progress against approved work plans and project targets.
  • Coordinate participant feedback, pre/post assessments, surveys, and other monitoring tools.
  • Document lessons learned, success stories, challenges, and good practices.
  • Work with relevant team members to use monitoring findings for continuous program improvement.

Reporting and Documentation

  • Prepare activity reports, meeting minutes, progress updates, participant records, and other project documentation.
  • Contribute to periodic narrative and donor reports.
  • Maintain organized digital and physical project records.
  • Ensure supporting documentation is complete and available for monitoring, reporting, auditing, and institutional learning.

Budget, Procurement and Administration Coordination

  • Coordinate with the Finance and Administration team on activity budgets, procurement requests, payments, travel, logistics, and supporting documentation.
  • Monitor activity-level expenditures in coordination with relevant team members.
  • Ensure program activities follow organizational procedures and donor requirements.

Communications and Outreach

  • Coordinate with the communications team to support project visibility, outreach, participant engagement, and dissemination.
  • Provide accurate program information, activity highlights, participant stories, and results for communication materials.
  • Support outreach to relevant institutions, networks, communities, and target beneficiaries.

GESI, Safeguarding and Compliance

  • Promote gender equality, social inclusion, accessibility, and meaningful participation of underrepresented groups across program activities.
  • Ensure project implementation follows organizational safeguarding, ethical, and data protection standards.
  • Support compliance with donor requirements, organizational policies, and relevant laws and regulations.

Required Qualifications and Experience

  • Minimum Bachelor’s degree in Development Studies, Management, Social Sciences, Public Administration, International Relations, Business Administration, Project Management, or another relevant discipline.
  • Preferably 3–5 years of relevant professional experience in program/project coordination, development programs, youth engagement, innovation, education, technology, governance, or related sectors.
  • Experience coordinating donor-funded or multi-stakeholder projects is preferred.
  • Experience organizing trainings, workshops, events, or capacity-building activities.
  • Experience in project documentation, monitoring, reporting, and stakeholder coordination.

Required Skills and Competencies

  • Strong program and project coordination skills.
  • Excellent organizational and time-management skills.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills in English and Nepali.
  • Ability to manage multiple activities and deadlines simultaneously.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and interpersonal skills.
  • Good report writing and documentation skills.
  • Working knowledge of monitoring, evaluation, and results tracking.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, and digital collaboration tools.
  • Ability to work collaboratively in multidisciplinary and multicultural teams.
  • Strong problem-solving, adaptability, and attention to detail.
  • Willingness to travel to project implementation areas when required.

Key Working Relationships

The Program Coordinator will work closely with:

  • Executive Director and Program Leadership
  • Project/Program Managers and Program Team
  • Finance and Administration Team
  • Communications Team
  • Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Team
  • Consultants, trainers, mentors, and technical experts
  • Partner organizations and consortium members
  • Government agencies, development partners, academic institutions, civil society organizations, private-sector actors, and participating communities

Performance Expectations

Performance will be assessed based on timely and quality implementation of assigned activities, achievement of project deliverables, stakeholder coordination, quality of documentation and reporting, compliance with organizational and donor requirements, effective teamwork, and contribution to overall program outcomes.

Equal Opportunity

Youth Innovation Lab is committed to equal opportunity, inclusion, and non-discrimination. All staff members are expected to uphold organizational values, safeguarding standards, professional ethics, and respectful workplace practices.

We are committed to promoting workforce diversity and strongly encourage applications from youth and young professionals, especially those who identify as women, members of indigenous communities, and minority caste groups.

Interviews will be conducted on a rolling basis. Therefore, we encourage interested candidates to apply at their earliest convenience. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for an interview.
! Due to the large number of applications received, we are unable to contact each applicant individually regarding the status of their application. Please be advised that if you do not receive any email, call, or contact from Youth Innovation Lab within three weeks from the date of the application deadline, you may consider yourself as not being selected for the position at this time.

Deadline for submission of application: 28 August 2026

Applying Procedure

Please click on Apply Now! button to submit your application. For more information on Youth Innovation Lab, please visit https://youthinnovationlab.org and if you have any inquiries, please contact at humanresource@youthinnovationlab.org.

Job Description

Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

  • Tier 0: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.
  • Tier 1: Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments
  • Tier 2: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers
  • Tier 3 or no tier indicated: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

As part of these efforts, UNDP, with anchor investment from partners such as the International Climate Initiative (IKI) of Germany and in consultation with several members of Tiger Conservation Coalition (TCC), is leading the development and operationalization of the Tiger Landscapes Investment Facility (TLIF). The Tiger Landscapes Investment Facility or TLIF is a blended finance mechanism developed in response to the urgent need to catalyze private sector investments into nature-positive businesses that contribute to the protection, restoration, and sustainable management of Tiger Landscapes.

The TLIF is uniquely structured to mobilize private sector capital predominantly from domestic financial institutions. The TLIF is structured to have two arms. The Technical Assistance Facility (TA facility) aims to work with the local stakeholders, conservation organizations, and institutions – government and private – to develop pipelines of investable projects. An innovative and fit-for-purpose guarantee facility – administered by the United Nations Capital Development Fund (UNCDF) – provided to the local financial institutions to enable lending to those pipelines of projects created through the support of the TA facility. The TLIF is also designed to have a unique governance structure that represents the donors, the investors and members of the Tiger Conservation Coalition (TCC).

Duties and Responsibilities

The National Project Specialist (NPS) will lead the coordination and management of the TA facility in Nepal. The incumbent will identify and engage with partners on pipeline development and coordinate with the Financial Service Providers (FSPs) to support the financing of the nature-positive projects. By the end of the project, a substantial number of enterprises are expected to have been established, contributing to the conservation and restoration of the tiger landscapes. In addition to that the NPS will contribute to the impact monitoring and evaluation, randomized verification, preparation of case studies and engagement with the government to further enhance the scale and impact of the Facility.

The NPS will lead the project and oversee day-to-day implementation of the TA Facility in Nepal under the direct supervision of the Portfolio Manager, Resilience and Environment Portfolio and in close coordination with the Global Project Manager of the TLIF as well as the Assistant Resident Representative (ARR) for Nepal. The NPS will be responsible for ensuring that project results are delivered in line with the approved project document, meeting agreed standards of quality, timeframes, and budget. Key duties include preparing annual work plans and budgets for approval, as well as semi-annual and annual progress reports outlining achievements, challenges, and necessary adjustments. The NPS will manage procurement and recruitment of national and international service providers and specialist expertise in consultation with the Global team and Country Office. The NPS will also play a central role in coordinating the efforts of all partners to ensure coherent and effective delivery.

Lead Project Coordination and Management

  • Develop annual work plans, budgets, and targets in line with the TLIF Project Document.
  • Monitor progress against plans, identify bottlenecks, and propose corrective measures to ensure timely and quality delivery.
  • Support UNDP with regular updates, background materials, and reporting for decision-making.
  • Lead and supervise the Project, setting clear objectives and providing performance guidance.
  • Oversee procurement, contracting, and recruitment processes, including drafting TORs and technical specifications.
  • Ensure the effective and accountable use of project resources in line with UNDP standards.
  • Identify, contract, and supervise consultants, suppliers, and service providers to ensure quality and timely delivery of outputs.
  • Coordinate and oversee the timely execution of project activities, consultants, and suppliers.
  • Monitor the quality of technical outputs, ensuring compliance with approved standards.
  • Establish and maintain systems for monitoring progress, risks, and results.
  • Prepare semi-annual and annual progress reports for submission to Global Team and CO.
  • Lead the implementation of project activities, ensuring the timely delivery of approved project outputs and coordination with responsible parties.
  • Coordinate annual and third-party verification processes and consolidate impact and other relevant reports as required by the donor, UNDP and the government partners.
  • Monitor project risks, provide updates on evolving or materialized risks, and propose mitigation and management actions.
  • Ensure compliance with project frameworks and funding requirements, especially UNDP’s Programme and Operations Policies and Procedures (POPP).

Lead Implementation of Technical Assistance Facility

  • Lead the establishment of pipeline development programme by identifying business service providers, specialised agencies, and conservation NGOs through a competitive process.
  • Lead the technical assistance to the financial service providers (FSPs), particularly in ensuring that the TLIF eligibility criteria are fit for purpose and are accurately applied as per the agreement between TLIF and the FSPs.
  • Engage pipeline development partners to enhance outreach to local enterprises to be developed.
  • Strengthen the capacity of the pipeline development partners, focusing on improving the biodiversity impact of the enterprises.
  • Establish and manage relevant advisory groups to enhance the competitiveness of the nature-positive enterprises
  • Facilitate exchanges between business service providers, conservation NGOs, specialized government agencies and Financial Service Providers (FSPs) to enhance financial and impact competitiveness of enterprises and increase the outreach to target beneficiaries.
  • Conduct field visits to potential and financed enterprises to monitor impact and provide strategic support for strengthening biodiversity-positive impact.
  • Coordinate with the Impact Investment Specialist to ensure FSPs have the necessary capacity to apply the Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), including the TLIF eligibility criteria, and monitor biodiversity impact.
  • Coordinate with the Impact Investment Specialist to ensure that the necessary financial literacy and capacity on finance among the business service providers, and the enterprises financed.

Build Strategic Partnerships, Stakeholder Engagement and Facilitate Knowledge Sharing

  • Serve as the central point of coordination and maintain strong working relationships with project partners at national, state, and community levels, ensuring effective liaison with government counterparts, UN agencies, and other responsible parties involved in implementation.
  • Ensure regular engagement with the government and other stakeholders to share updates, challenges and opportunities.
  • Maintain good relationships with key stakeholders, including government agencies, private sector partners, financial institutions, conservation organizations including the members of the Tiger Conservation Coalition, and local communities within tiger landscapes.
  • Organize, facilitate, and/or participate in events, meetings, workshops and conferences to enhance the profile of the TLIF and to engage stakeholders.
  • Support the south-south exchange and participation of the government in relevant events.
  • Support knowledge-sharing and learning efforts to enhance the effectiveness of the Tiger Landscapes Investment Facility.
  • Support project visibility and communications activities in coordination with UNDP and national partners.
  • Promote knowledge exchange and capacity development with Government counterparts and local stakeholders.
  • Document and disseminate lessons learned and best practices within Nepal and across region.

Mainstreaming Gender Equality and Social Inclusion:

  • Ensure mainstreaming of Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI) principles throughout project planning, implementation, monitoring, and reporting in line with national policies and UNDP’s gender and social safeguards requirements.
  • Facilitate the integration of gender-responsive and inclusive climate actions in project interventions, ensuring that women, indigenous peoples, persons with disabilities, and marginalized groups actively participate and benefit equitably.
  • Promote capacity development on GESI and climate resilience for project staff, implementing partners, and local stakeholders, ensuring inclusive participation and gender-balanced representation.
  • Ensure that data collection and reporting are sex-, age-, and disability-disaggregated, and that progress reports adequately reflect gender equality and social inclusion outcomes.
  • Identify and address potential gender and social risks associated with project activities, proposing mitigation measures in coordination with relevant stakeholders.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The National Project Specialist will head the Project Unit and oversee day-to-day implementation of the TA Facility in Nepal. The NPS will function as the Project Manager for TLIF in accordance with UNDP’s Internal Control Framework under the direct supervision of the Portfolio Manager (Resilience and Environment). The NPS is required to work in close coordination with the Global Project Manager of the TLIF as well as under the guidance from the Assistant Resident Representative (Resilience and Environment Portfolio) for Nepal.

  •  Support the Senior Construction Manager in developing and updating project work plans, construction schedules, and activity trackers.
  •  Coordinate procurement requests, material deliveries, and site logistics with the procurement/admin team, suppliers, and contractors.
  • Assist in reviewing construction drawings, Bills of Quantities (BoQs), cost estimates, and material specifications for accuracy before implementation.
  • Track daily and weekly progress against schedules, and flag delays, resource gaps, or bottlenecks to the Senior Construction Manager.

Site Monitoring, Quality & Safety Support — 30%

  •  Conduct regular site visits to monitor progress, workmanship, and adherence to approved designs and technical standards.
  •  Support quality checks at key construction stages site preparation, foundation, masonry, roofing, and finishing and document findings.
  • Monitor site-level compliance with the Nepal National Building Code, safety protocols, and organisational policies.
  • Monitor the usage, storage, and security of construction materials and equipment at work sites.
  • Identify and report site-level issues, risks, and variations promptly, and support the Senior Construction Manager in implementing corrective actions.

Stakeholder & Community Coordination — 20%

  •  Serve as the day-to-day point of contact between UWS Nepal, contractors, sub-engineers, and local site supervisors.
  •  Support coordination with ward offices, municipalities, and local government authorities for permits, inspections, and approvals.
  • Coordinate with Local Government, School Management Committees (SMCs), teachers, and community members to facilitate smooth, inclusive, and conflict-free implementation.
  • Organise and document site coordination meetings, stakeholder consultations, and technical discussions.

Documentation, Reporting & Financial Tracking — 10%

  •  Maintain accurate, up-to-date site records, including daily progress reports, site photographs, inspection checklists, and meeting minutes.
  •  Support tracking of project expenditures, contractor bills, and material invoices, ensuring accuracy and proper documentation.
  • Compile and submit timely weekly/monthly progress, technical, and financial reports to theSupervisor.
  • Maintain well-organised project files, both physical and digital, for internal reporting and audit purposes.

Team & Administrative Support — 10%

  •  Provide day-to-day coordination and support to site-level staff, labourers, and subcontractors.
  •  Lead training, orientation, for construction team including safety briefings for site teams.
  •  Promote a safety-first culture by ensuring site staff and labourers follow proper safety procedures.
  • Perform other duties as assigned by the supervisor.

Required Skills & Qualifications

Education & Experience

  •  Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering.
  • At least 3-4 years of relevant experience in construction coordination, site supervision, or project support, preferably on infrastructure or school-building projects.
  • Prior working experience on education/school construction projects in the not-for-profitsector.

Technical Skills

  • Working knowledge of construction processes, materials, and methods, including foundation, masonry, roofing, and finishing works.
  • Familiarity with the Nepal National Building Code, construction safety standards, and quality assurance practices.
  • Ability to read and interpret construction drawings, BoQs, and technical specifications.
  • Basic proficiency in MS Office (Word, Excel) for reporting, tracking, and documentation; familiarity with AutoCAD or similar tools is a plus.
  • Understanding of construction budgeting, procurement processes, and basic financial tracking.

Core Competencies & Soft Skills

  • Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple sites, tasks, and timelines simultaneously.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills to coordinate effectively with contractors, engineers, government officials, and communities.
  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy in site monitoring, documentation, and reporting.
  •  Ability to work independently in the field while maintaining close communication with the Senior Construction Manager.
  • Willingness to travel frequently to project sites, including remote locations.
  •  Commitment to UWS Nepal’s mission, values, and child-safeguarding policies.

Job Title : Construction Officer
Department : Programmeme

ROLE SUMMARY

The Construction Officer is responsible for ensuring the successful, timely, and cost-effective completion of school construction projects in rural areas of Nepal, ensuring compliance with Nepal National Building Codes and local regulations; monitoring progress against schedule and budget; maintaining strong communication and coordination among stakeholders; safeguarding site safety and security; and providing technical guidance and expertise to construction teams.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Visit proposed sites to assess feasibility and prepare required documentation.

2. Work with Architects/Engineers to review and approve construction plans, ensuring compliance with design, regulatory, and local requirements.

3. Prepare construction schedules, cost estimates, and material specifications.

4. Supervise construction activities to ensure compliance with approved plans, specifications, and building codes.

5. Track project progress, identify risks or delays, and take corrective action; manage resources and monitor spending against budget to ensure timely, within-budget completion.

6. Set up Construction Coordination Committees (CCC) in each community and coordinate with local authorities, communities, and stakeholders to secure permits, clearances, and utilities, and to support local participation and ownership.

7. Guide contractors and construction teams on technical issues, resolving queries and promoting quality workmanship.

8. Enforce safety measures and carry out inspections and quality checks to ensure adherence to construction standards.

9. Hold regular progress meetings with stakeholders to communicate updates and resolve issues.

10. Maintain accurate records (site logs, measurements, change orders, as-built drawings) per the UWS Construction Manual, and submit weekly progress reports on status, budget, and deviations.

11. Manage handover of completed school buildings to relevant authorities.

QUALIFICATION, EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS

  • Diploma in Civil Engineering from a recognized institution / CTEVT certificate in the related field.

  •  Proficiency in office software packages (MS Word, Excel, Google Suite, etc.)
  •  Working knowledge about computer aided drafting software like AutoCAD or ArchiCAD etc.
  •  Understanding and experience in remote rural areas of Nepal.
  • Ability to build and maintain positive relationships with community stakeholders.
  • Good problem-solving and organizational skills.

Himalayan Life Insurance Company Limited, one of Nepal’s leading life insurance companies, invites applications from highly accomplished, dynamic, visionary and result-oriented professionals for the position of Chief Executive Officer (CEO).

The Chief Executive Officer will be responsible for providing overall strategic and executive leadership to the Company, driving sustainable business growth and profitability, strengthening the Company’s market position, and ensuring operational excellence, sound corporate governance and regulatory compliance.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Provide strategic direction and overall leadership to the Company in line with the vision and objectives established by the Board of Directors.
  • Drive sustainable growth in business, premium income, profitability and market share.
  • Lead and strengthen the Company’s sales and distribution network, particularly the agency force, to enhance productivity, quality of business and long-term customer retention.
  • Develop and execute strategies for effective agent recruitment, development, motivation, productivity and retention.
  • Strengthen life insurance operations, including underwriting, claims management, product development, customer service and distribution.
  • Ensure prudent financial, investment, risk and capital management of the Company.
  • Maintain strong corporate governance, risk management, internal control and regulatory compliance.
  • Develop a high-performing management team and foster a performance-driven organizational culture.
  • Maintain effective relationships with the Board of Directors, Nepal Insurance Authority, shareholders, customers, employees, agents and other stakeholders.

QUALIFICATION AND EXPERIENCE

  • Meet all eligibility, qualification, experience, fit-and-proper and other requirements prescribed for the Chief Executive Officer of a life insurance company under the prevailing Insurance Act, regulations, directives and guidelines issued by the Nepal Insurance Authority.
  • Possess a Master’s Degree or equivalent in Management, Business Administration, Finance, Economics, Accounting, Insurance or other relevant discipline from recognized university institution, or be a qualified Chartered Accountant (CA) from a recognized professional accounting body.
  • Have substantial relevant experience in the life insurance industry, including at least five (5) years of experience in the position of Deputy Chief Executive Officer (DCEO) and/or Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of a life insurance company.
  • Have demonstrated senior executive leadership experience with proven ability to formulate and execute corporate strategy and manage a large and complex life insurance business.
  • Possess strong and demonstrated knowledge and experience in life insurance sales, distribution and agency force management, including agent recruitment, development, productivity, retention and performance management.
  • Have sound knowledge of life insurance operations, products, underwriting, claims, reinsurance, risk management, investment, financial management and regulatory compliance.
  • Possess a thorough understanding of Nepal’s life insurance market, regulatory environment, corporate governance requirements and emerging trends in the insurance sector.
  • Demonstrate strong leadership, strategic thinking, decision-making, communication and stakeholder-management capabilities.

APPLICATION PROCESS

Interested and eligible candidates are requested to submit their application no later than 26th August 2026.

Applications shall be addressed to the Board of Directors and submitted by email to recruitment.hli2026@gmail.com along with the following:

  • Application/Cover Letter

  • Copies of relevant academic and professional credentials
  • Documents supporting the required professional experience
  • A comprehensive Business Plan for Himalayan Life Insurance Company Limited, outlining the candidate’s strategic vision, business growth priorities, sales and distribution strategy, agency force development, operational improvement, profitability, governance and proposed roadmap for the Company.

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for further assessment and interview. The Company reserves the right to accept or reject any application without assigning any reason. All applications and information received will be treated with strict confidentiality.

Posiiton: Production & QC Head
Location: Kathmandu

Job Summary

The QC & Production Head is responsible for managing overall production and quality operations. The role ensures timely production as per sales demand while maintaining quality standards, optimizing resources, and ensuring compliance with food safety and company procedures. The incumbent oversees production planning, quality control, batch-wise production, pest control, labor management, and cross-functional coordination.

Key Responsibilities

1. Production Planning & Operations

  • Prepare daily, weekly, and monthly production plans based on sales forecasts and customer demand.
  • Ensure timely execution of production schedules while optimizing manpower, machinery, and resources.
  • Monitor batch-wise production to ensure accuracy, traceability, and adherence to production standards.
  • Coordinate with Sales, Procurement, and Stores to ensure uninterrupted production.
  • Continuously improve production efficiency and minimize downtime.

2. Quality Control & Quality Assurance

  • Develop, implement, and monitor quality standards across all manufacturing processes.
  • Conduct quality inspections of raw materials before production.
  • Ensure in-process quality checks during production.
  • Verify finished goods quality before dispatch or storage.
  • Investigate quality issues, identify root causes, and implement corrective and preventive actions (CAPA).
  • Maintain product consistency across all batches.

3. Raw Material & Finished Goods Quality

  • Approve incoming raw materials based on defined quality parameters.
  • Ensure proper storage and handling of raw materials and finished goods.
  • Monitor product shelf life, packaging quality, and overall product standards.
  • Coordinate with suppliers regarding quality-related issues whenever required.

4. Production Coordination

  • Coordinate with Sales to understand demand forecasts and priority orders.
  • Work closely with Procurement to ensure timely availability of raw materials.
  • Coordinate with Warehouse and Logistics for smooth dispatch of finished goods.
  • Ensure production targets are achieved without compromising quality.

5. Pest Control & Hygiene Compliance

  • Supervise pest control activities across all production and storage areas.
  • Ensure implementation of food safety, hygiene, sanitation, and housekeeping standards.
  • Maintain records of pest control inspections and corrective actions.
  • Ensure compliance with internal quality standards and applicable regulatory requirements.

6. Labor Management

  • Plan and allocate labor according to production requirements.
  • Monitor labor productivity and attendance.
  • Coordinate with HR for labor onboarding, documentation, deployment, and compliance.
  • Ensure proper discipline, safety practices, and adherence to company policies on the production floor.

7. Documentation & Compliance

  • Maintain batch manufacturing records and quality documentation.
  • Ensure proper documentation of production reports, quality reports, and inspection records.
  • Support internal and external quality audits.
  • Ensure compliance with applicable food safety, manufacturing, and statutory regulations.

8. Continuous Improvement

  • Identify opportunities to improve production efficiency, product quality, and cost optimization.
  • Reduce wastage, rework, and production losses through process improvements.
  • Introduce best practices and standard operating procedures (SOPs) for continuous operational excellence.

Qualification

  • Bachelor’s degree in food technology, Food Science, Industrial Engineering, Production Management, Quality Management, or related discipline.
  • Additional certifications in Quality Management, HACCP, GMP, ISO, or Food Safety will be an advantage.

Experience

  • 7–10 years of experience in production and quality management within the FMCG, food manufacturing, packaging, or related manufacturing industry.
  • Experience managing multiple production units or manufacturing plants is preferred.
