  • Functional Title: Internal Audit Officer
  • Responsibility Level: Officer
  • Department: Internal Audit
  • Workstation: Kathmandu
  • Incumbent’s Name: To Be Determined
  • Supervisor/Principal: Internal Audit Specialist

 JOB SUMMARY

The Internal Audit Officer will be primarily responsible for performing the internal audit of grants, functions, and partners independently with minimum supervision from the Internal Audit Specialist to provide an independent appraisal of CARE Nepal’s financial, program/project, operational and control activities. The Internal Audit Officer will be specifically responsible for 1) supporting for the internal audit plan & risk assessment for fiscal year in close consultation with Internal Audit Specialist; 2) leading the audit team to perform the audit as per the approved plan and provide report which includes control weakness, root cause of the problem and reasonable recommendations to address the gaps/non-compliance for issues identified; 3) prepare a database of the partners based on the risk assessment of the partner by using the information obtained from Sub Grants and Finance unit and considering other performance indicators; 4) facilitating entire audits i.e. project, mission, donor and any other relevant reviews; 5) assisting Internal Audit Specialist to perform special review as required by ARMU and CARE USA.

The employee shall fully comply with CARE policies and procedures and should be accountable for it.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND TASKS:

R1. Auditing

  • Independently perform periodic audits of different grants, functions, departments, and partner organizations based on a systematic and risk/exposure methodology as per the internal audit plan.
  • Support the Internal Audit Specialist in preparation of annual audit plan focusing on the materiality/risk level.
  • Perform surprise audits in close coordination with the Internal Audit Specialist of CARE and Partners in order to review the adequacy and effectiveness of internal control and systems implemented by CARE Nepal and partner NGOs. Provide appropriate feedback for strengthening their systems/policies and contribute to their capacity building.
  • Provide a written report based on the audit that includes control gaps, root causes, and recommendations linked with the gaps in order to provide support to the management to overcome the gaps. While performing the audit, proper consideration should be given to CARE USA asserted controls, donor requirements, government regulations, and CARE Nepal policies/procedures.
  • Assist the Internal Audit Specialist to conduct special or requested audit/review as required by CARE Nepal Management, ARMU, CARE Headquarters, and Internal Audit in Atlanta.
  • Facilitate the timely completion of the external/project/donor audit. Review the audit requirements of all projects, prepare an audit tracker based on the audit requirements for the fiscal year, develop project- specific Terms of Reference (TOR), and coordinate with CARE Management and the external auditor for timely completion of the audit.
  • Assist in the investigation with the support and guidance from the Internal Audit Specialist and CUSA investigation team.

R2. Capacity Building & Partner Risk Assessment

  • Rigorous follow-up to review implementation status of corrective action plan prepared by the management based on the recommendations of different audits and provide assurance that implemented changes adequately resolved audit findings. Monthly reporting to the Internal Audit Specialist about the status of any unresolved issues.
  • Preparing different training materials and a capacity development plan to help the management to address the control gaps identified during the time of audit, under the close supervision of the Internal Audit Specialist.
  • Perform analytical procedures and risk ranking of the partners as per the risk assessment process. Update the risk ranking on a periodic basis so that CARE management has a proper understanding of the risk level of all the partners.
  • Assess financial and operational capacity of PNGOs through periodic visit/walk through test and random document review.
  • Perform any other relevant jobs which will not impact on the independence of the internal audit function.

R3. Upholding CARE’s Core values and ensuring its principles.

  • Link and demonstrate CARE Nepal’s core values, programming principles, strategic objects, women and girls’ equality, and impact in programming and behaviors.
  • Comply and exercise organizational values and culture.
  • Help to promote rights and good governance.
  • Responsive to women and girls’ specific needs in all actions and decisions.
  • Safety and Security is everyone’s responsibility within CI through full compliance and accountability (as per Principle-ii of the CARE International Safety & Security Principles).
  • Any other duties/responsibilities as per the need/priority of mission in consultation with supervisor.

 AUTHORITY:

Spending authority: NA

 Working conditions: Based in Kathmandu

Qualifications and Experience

Professional accountancy certification (ACCA/CA/CPA) with at least 3 years of experience or semi qualified certification/bachelor’s in business administration, finance, or equivalent with at least 5 years of experience. Prior experience in investigation in the development sector (I/NGO) is desirable.

 Knowledge Skills and Competencies

Required Skills:

  • Strong knowledge and experience of auditing procedures and practices of NGO and INGOs.
  • Knowledge and experience in financial and administrative procedures
  • Good understanding of the rules and regulations of GON related to income tax and other issues.

content.rendered:
The Gurkha Welfare Trust Nepal is the field arm of The Gurkha Welfare Trust UK, a charitable Trust established and registered in the UK in 1969, and working particularly for the ex-Gurkha Veterans
and their communities across Nepal.

We are seeking applications from suitably qualified, committed, and eligible individuals for the following positions:

1. Vehicle Mechanic/Mechanical Transport Assistant based at this Trust’s Headquarters (HQ) in Pokhara.
2. Project Supervisor based at HQ Project Cell initially. Area Welfare Centre (AWC) to be confirmed in due course.
3. Cluster Pharmacist based in AWC Butwal.

1. VEHICLE MECHANIC/MECHANICAL TRANSPORT ASSISTANT:

Key Responsibilities:

The Vehicle Mechanic/MT Asst delivers integrated technical, coordination, and senior driving support to ensure the organisation’s fleet remains safe, roadworthy, and consistently operational.
The role provides in-house preventive maintenance, diagnostics, repairs, and independent technical assessments, ensuring that referral to external garages occurs only when necessary and following rigorous technical and cost scrutiny. It plans and monitors maintenance schedules, oversees and quality assures outsourced repairs, verifies costings, and maintains accurate fleet, safety, and
compliance records.

This role also undertakes senior driving duties and mentors drivers across GWT(N), promoting safe driving practices, regulatory compliance, efficient fleet utilisation, and reduced downtime, costs, and operational disruption in line with duty of care standards.

Please read through the Job Description for further information on job responsibilities.

Essential and Desirable Criteria:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Automobile Engineering, Mechanical Engineering.
  • Minimum 3 years’ practical experience in vehicle maintenance and repair (4WD vehicles minimum and motorbikes preferred).
  •  Must have a valid Nepali driving license of Categories A and B. In possession of category ‘F’ driving license is desirable.
  •  Ability to diagnose mechanical faults systematically and be familiar with preventive maintenance scheduling.
  •  Strong knowledge of petrol and diesel engines with knowledge of electrical systems, suspension, braking systems, and transmission.
  •  Must be computer-literate, able to use MS Office (Word, Excel, and PowerPoint).
  •  Should have very good leadership, management and interpersonal skills.
  •  Should have work ethics, resourcefulness, integrity and dedication to duties.
  • Experience with NGO/INGO Equipment Care and fleet management will be an advantage.

2. PROJECT SUPERVISOR:

Key Responsibilities:

The Project Supervisor will undertake field visits to flat, hilly, and remote areas of Nepal to carry out technical site surveys for school construction projects, new house construction, and house enhancement works.
The Project Supervisor may be based either at the Headquarters (Project Cell) or on Area Welfare Centres (AWCs), depending on project workload, geographic coverage, and the nature of the assigned projects. Frequent travel to project locations will be required to ensure effective implementation, monitoring, and reporting of project activities.

Please read through the Job Description for further information on job responsibilities.

Essential and Desirable Criteria:

  • Diploma in Civil Engineering with at least 3 years of work experience in supervising construction projects. Alternatively, Sub-overseer in civil engineering with 6 years of work experience.
  •  Computer literacy, including word processing.
  •  Knowledge of working with AutoCAD and other design packages.
  •  Experience working within a government department, INGO, or NGO in Nepal.
  •  Must be in possession of category ‘A’ Nepali driving license with experience on riding rough terrains.
  •  In possession of category ‘B’ driving license is desirable.
  •  Experience on WASH related programmes will be an advantage.

3. CLUSTER PHARMACIST:

Key Responsibilities:

The Cluster Pharmacist is overall responsible for implementing Pharmacy related Clinical Care and Clinical Governance in his/her Medical Centre in accordance with all GWT(N) SIs, Standards of Medical Service delivery, Quality Standards, Policies and Procedures. The Cluster pharmacist is responsible for the Pharmacy Service delivery and management at Key AWC’s, non-Key AWC’s and patrol bases in liaison with Healthcare Professional’s in the medical centres.

Please read through the Job Description for further information on job responsibilities.

Essential and Desirable Criteria:

  • Minimum of Bachelor’s Degree in Pharmacy with at least 2 years of work experience post qualification.
  • Current unrestricted registration as a Pharmacist with Nepal Pharmacy Council (NPC).
  • Must be computer literate and should have knowledge of Pharmacy Inventory software.
  • Working knowledge and application of relevant Country legislation governing Pharmacy Service Delivery.
  •  Ability to work independently and as part of a team, paying careful attention to detail and managing multiple tasks.
  • High level of communication skills.
  • Experience in reputed private hospitals/ community pharmacy an advantage.
  • Prior Experience working with international organisations will be an advantage.
  • Able to work effectively with both medical and non-medical staff.

REMUNERATION

All three positions fall in EG3L1 in our pay structure, with a basic monthly salary of NPR 76,571.
Current salary is applicable for internal candidates transferring level.
All other benefits and facilities will be provided in accordance with GWT(N) Standing Instructions.
The initial contract duration is three years (two years for Project Supervisor position), with the possibility of extension based on organisational needs and individual performance.

ELIGIBILITY AND APPLICATIONS

Qualified, eligible, and interested applicants are invited to submit their applications by Wednesday,26 August 2026.

For Vehicle Mechanic/Mechanical Transport Assistant position, click here to apply.
For Project Supervisor position, click here to apply.
For Cluster Pharmacist position, click here to apply.

Internal candidates are to refer to Chapters 6.10.17 to 6.10.20 of the SI for details regarding eligibility criteria for level transfer and promotion.

Only applications submitted online will be accepted. Applications sent via email will be discarded.

Telephone inquiries will not be entertained.

The Gurkha Welfare Trust Nepal is an equal opportunity employer

Position: Program Coordinator

Job Overview

The Program Coordinator is responsible for providing academic and administrative leadership for the assigned academic programs. The position ensures the effective delivery of academic activities, faculty management, student success initiatives, examination management, admissions, industry collaboration, compliance, and overall program development. The Program Coordinator shall work towards achieving academic excellence, operational efficiency, stakeholder satisfaction, and sustainable growth of the program.

Major Duties and Responsibilities

Academic Management

  • Oversee syllabus and micro syllabus design, implementation, review, and improvement.
  • Ensure effective teaching and learning practices and academic quality standards.
  • Develop annual academic calendars and academic plans.
  • Introduce and implement non-credit and skill enhancement programs.
  • Monitor academic performance and program outcomes.

Faculty Management

  • Supervise faculty workload and performance.
  • Conduct faculty performance evaluations.
  • Organize faculty development and training programs.
    Support recruitment, orientation, and retention of faculty members.

Student Affairs

  • Monitor student progress, attendance, retention, and academic performance.
  • Organize academic counseling, mentoring, and career development activities.
  • Manage student clubs, ECA, and CCA activities.
  • Coordinate internship and placement activities.
  • Resolve student grievances and disciplinary matters.

Examination Management

  • Plan and supervise internal examinations, practical examinations, and viva voce.
  • Ensure timely publication of examination results.
  • Prepare and submit internal evaluation marks to the university.
  • Maintain the accuracy and confidentiality of examination records.

Administration and Operations

  • Supervise the day-to-day operational activities of the program.
  • Prepare academic and administrative reports.
  • Coordinate logistics and resource management.
  • Draft policies, procedures, prospectus, and academic documents.

Stakeholder Engagement

  • Maintain relationships with students, parents, alumni, industries, universities, and professional bodies.
  • Establish industry partnerships and facilitate internship opportunities.
  • Organize seminars, conferences, workshops, and guest lectures.

Admissions and Marketing

  • Lead admission counseling activities.
  • Conduct presentations for prospective students.
  • Support entrance examinations and preparatory classes.
  • Verify and support marketing and promotional activities.

Budget & Resource Management

  • Prepare and manage the annual departmental budget in coordination with management.
  • Ensure effective utilization of financial, physical, and academic resources.
  • Monitor resource requirements and recommend procurement to support academic and operational activities.

Reporting and Compliance

  • Submit regular reports to management.
  • Ensure compliance with university, UGC, and institutional requirements.
  • Conduct faculty meetings and maintain proper documentation.

Performance Measurements

i. Academic Excellence & Curriculum Management: 100% of syllabus and micro syllabus reviewed annually, academic calendar published before the commencement of the academic year, minimum 95% university pass rate, zero scheduling conflicts, and at least one new skill enhancement or non-credit program launched annually.

ii. Faculty Leadership & Student Success: 100% faculty appraisal completed, at least 90% of faculty meeting performance standards, a minimum of one faculty development program per semester, a student retention rate of at least 95%, and a student satisfaction score of at least 80%.

iii. Examination & Operational Management: Zero critical errors in examination results and university submissions, timely publication of internal examination results,
Submission of all required reports within deadlines, effective day-to-day operations, and implementation of approved academic policies and procedures.

iv. Industry Engagement, Placement & Program Growth: Minimum of five industry partnerships or MOUs annually, placement rate of at least 80%, minimum of two
seminars/workshops/guest lectures annually, growth in student enrollment, and increased internship opportunities for students.

v. Admissions, Compliance & Reporting: Achievement of approved enrollment targets, successful admission counseling and promotional activities, 100% compliance with university and institutional requirements, Effective utilization of resources within approved budget, timely submission of daily and weekly reports, and effective conduct of faculty and academic meetings.

Job Specifications

Education and Experience

  • At least MPhill Degree relevant discipline from a recognized university.
  • Minimum 5 to 7 years of teaching experience in higher education.
  • Minimum 10 years of experience in academic administration, program coordination, or leadership roles, including at least 5 years in a leadership position at a Tribhuvan University-affiliated college.

Knowledge, Skills, and Competencies

  • University regulations, academic policies, and quality assurance requirements.
  • Academic planning, curriculum development, and examination management systems.
  • Student support and placement practices.
  • Educational administration and stakeholder management.
  • Leadership and team management.
  • Strategic planning and decision making.
  • Communication and presentation skills.
  • Problem solving and conflict resolution.
  • Report writing and documentation.
  • Organizational and coordination skills.
  • High level of integrity and professionalism.
  • Commitment to academic excellence.
  • Confidentiality and ethical conduct.
  • Results-oriented and proactive approach.
  • Adaptability and willingness to undertake additional responsibilities.

Application Expiry Date: 2026-08-30

POSITION TITLE: Capacity Building Specialist
NUMBER OF POSITION: 1
DUTY STATION: Kathmandu with frequent field travel
REPORTS TO: Team Leader
DURATION: Until project period (11 months tentatively)

About Winrock International

Winrock International has been working in Nepal to increase access to clean energy through public awareness raising and capacity building since the establishment of Winrock International Nepal in 1997. Its work focuses on project design and implementation, technology and market assessments, developing project pipelines and mobilizing investments, reforming energy planning and policy, and building capacity of governments, communities, financial institutions, and the private sector. It provides Results-Focused, Human-Centered, Science-Based and Market-Driven technical and financial assistance.

Project Description

Winrock International is currently implementing a project across 3 provinces Bagmati, Gandaki, and Lumbini covering 10 districts: Nawalparasi (East and West of Bardaghat Susta), Palpa, Tanahun, Chitwan, Dhading, Makawanpur, Nuwakot, Sindhupalchowk, and Kathmandu.

The project aims to support productive use of energy, enhance enterprise competitiveness, and create employment opportunities in project affected wards and municipalities in these districts. Key interventions include:

Development and endorsement of 30 Municipal Energy Plans (MEPs)
Business training to 792 entrepreneurs to strengthen PUE-based enterprises
Skills training to 1,200 individuals, with strong focus on women, youth, and marginalized groups
Post-training support, including skill testing, job placement facilitation, business advisory services, and refresher sessions

Position Description

The Capacity Building Specialist will oversee the design, implementation, monitoring, and quality assurance of CTEVT Level 1 Skill Trainings and capacity-building interventions under the project. The position will support the management of training service providers, coordinate trainee selection processes, ensure alignment with CTEVT standards and curricula, and strengthen partnerships among government agencies, municipalities, training institutions, employers, and other stakeholders.

The Capacity Building Specialist will have key considerations on Social Analysis perspective throughout all training and capacity-building activities and contribute to monitoring, learning, and reporting requirements.

Main Duties and Responsibilities:

Under the overall guidance and the immediate supervision of Team Leader, the Capacity Building Specialist will be responsible for:

A. Capacity Building and Training Management

  • Lead the planning, coordination, and implementation of project-supported capacity building and skills development activities.
  • Develop and refine trainee selection criteria in coordination with project partners, municipalities, and relevant government agencies.
  • Ensure training programs are market-driven, demand-responsive, and aligned with employer needs.
  • Verify that all training programs comply with CTEVT Level 1 standards, curricula, and relevant government regulations.
  • Monitor training delivery to ensure quality standards are maintained.
  • Ensure adequate training materials, equipment, and learning resources are in place before commencement of training activities.
  • Lead the development and implementation of post-training support activities of National Skill Testing Board (NSTB) test and job placement and self-employment of graduate trainees to enhance employment and enterprise outcomes.

B. Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL)

  • Develop and implement training monitoring plans in alignment with project monitoring and evaluation frameworks.
  • Design and maintain training monitoring tools, indicators, and data collection systems.
  • Integrate Social Analysis indicators into monitoring processes.
  • Conduct regular field visits and monitoring of pre-training, training, and post-training activities.
  • Collect, analyze, and report training performance data and learning outcomes.
  • Prepare periodic progress reports, technical updates, success stories, and case studies.

C. Market Assessment and Employment Linkages

  • Assess emerging employment and entrepreneurship opportunities relevant to target beneficiaries.
  • Facilitate linkages between training graduates and potential employers.
  • Collaborate with private sector actors to strengthen workforce placement and internship opportunities.
  • Support enterprise development initiatives where relevant.

D. Stakeholder Coordination and Partnership Management

  • Coordinate closely with municipalities, government agencies, training institutions, employers, and other stakeholders.
  • Foster productive working relationships with beneficiary representatives and project partners.
  • Organize stakeholder consultations, workshops, and coordination meetings.
  • Support joint monitoring and field visits with donor representatives and key stakeholders as required.
  • Represent the project in technical meetings and sector coordination forums when assigned.

E. Social Analysis (SA)

  • Ensure Social Analysis considerations are integrated into all training and capacity building activities.
  • Promote participation of all populations.
  • Support collection and reporting of disaggregated data in accordance with project requirements.
  • Recommend measures to improve equitable access to training and employment opportunities.

F. Documentation and Reporting

  • Prepare technical reports, monitoring reports, and activity summaries.
  • Document lessons learned, best practices, success stories, and impact narratives.
  • Maintain accurate records of training activities, participant data, and monitoring findings.
  • Provide technical inputs to project work plans, annual reports, and donor deliverables.

G. Ethics, Safeguarding and Compliance

  • Comply with Donor’s and Winrock International’s policies and procedures, including ethics, safeguarding, security, and code of conduct requirements.
  • Complete all required organizational compliance training.
  • Ensure all activities are implemented in accordance with donor regulations and project guidelines.

Educational Qualification and Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Humanities, Social Sciences, Sociology, Social Work, Gender Studies, Development Studies, Rural Development, Education, or related field. Master’s degree in relevant field and TVET related qualification is preferable.
  • Minimum ten (10) years of professional experience in Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), workforce development, capacity building, or enterprise development.
  • At least two (2) years of experience conducting labor market assessments, market opportunity analysis, or enterprise development initiatives.
  • Demonstrated experience in training management, monitoring, and stakeholder coordination.
  • Experience working with municipalities, government agencies, development partners, and training institutions.
  • Experience integrating Social Analysis approaches into development programs.

Skills and Knowledge:

  • Strong understanding of Nepal’s TVET sector and CTEVT, NSTB systems.
  • Excellent planning, facilitation, training, and coordination skills.
  • Strong analytical, monitoring, and reporting capabilities.
  • Ability to manage multiple stakeholders and work effectively in multidisciplinary teams.
  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills.
  • Fluency in spoken and written English and Nepali.
  • Willingness and ability to travel frequently within Nepal.

Other:

  • Willingness to work as part of a team and a diverse group of people is essential.
  • Ability to always demonstrate the highest level of ethical standards.
  • Ability to work under pressure and handle multiple projects.

To Apply: Interested candidates are requested to send a cover letter, updated CV and list of three references by 31 August 2026, to winrocknepal@winrock.org

Application from Female and disadvantage group is highly appreciated.

Please note that only short-listed candidates will be contacted, and phone inquiries will not be entertained.

Position: Donor Contract Management and Reporting Coordinator (INT11767)
Location: Nepal – Kathmandu
Workplace Type: On-site
Hours:40
Salary: As per Nepal National Pay scale
Job Family: Programme
Division: International
Grade: National D1
Job Type: Fixed Term
Closing Date: 27 August 2026
Country: Nepal

Oxfam is a global movement of people working together to end the injustice of poverty.

The Role:

Oxfam Nepal is looking for Donor Contract Management and Reporting Coordinator , Coordinate and oversee the end-to-end management of donor contracts and grants, ensuring effective coordination and maintenance of contractual relationships with donors and Partner Affiliates (PAs). Facilitate compliance with donor requirements, proactively identify and escalate contract risks, and support timely corrective actions, including amendments and extensions. Ensure high-quality and timely donor and organisational reporting, income accounting, contract opening and closure processes, and contribute to effective Contract Management Reviews (CMR). Collaborate closely with Country Leadership and Management Team (CLMT), budget holders, and the EA Node to strengthen grant and project management processes, including the effective use of OPAL and CRIMSON systems, while maintaining regular communication and updates with key donors and stakeholders.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES (Technical, Leadership, People and Resource management)

Contract Cycle Management 40%

  • Reviews new and amended Oxfam Project Agreement (OPA) and share it with EA node for endorsement.
  • Facilitates and coordinates Oxfam Project Agreement (OPA) discussions and negotiations for new and secured grants with Oxfam affiliates.
  • Summarize contract clauses for Budget Holders/Project Manager after it is signed off.
  • Accountable for keeping the donor and Oxfam Affiliates member informed of any significant issue on secured contract and for addressing these.
  • For secured contract coordinate and share programme and donor information with programmes and finance staff, regional centre, OGB/EA , OI and other Oxfam affiliates as appropriate and as may be requested.
  • Manages the contractual relationship with the donor/member through communication on reports, and contracts update
  • Lead on institutional fund secured contract management and liaise with affiliates with regards to Oxfam Project Agreement (OPA) amendment, net funding figures and reporting. (e.g. processing grant agreements and contracts, including GIK)
  • Create and Maintain contract award files in CRIMSON for new/current contracts which is Oxfam’s contract management platform and provides support in OPAL, as country focal person, which is Oxfam’s project management platform.
  • Ensure year-wise budget phasing is updated in CRIMSON in coordination with Budget Holders and Head of Business Support.
  • Ensure proper income accounting is done and track and raise Income in the system and regular follow up until income is realized when it is due to ensure smooth income from donors to the project.
  • For the purpose of filing, record donor issues and communications, record Finance, HR and Supply Chain close-out processes, donor audit, as required and record all deliberations on close-out and coordinate with Budget Holder, Business Support and Impact and PQ team for support
  • Throughout the implementation of the contract, ensure that all award information is shared effectively with relevant staff across the organization and partners.
  • Ensure that Budget Holders/ designated delegate upload all the reports, publications and documentations under the project are filed in OPAL for respective project.
  • Bring major issues/ risks in current contract management to the attention of Country Director, respective Budget Holder and Country Leadership and Management Team.
  • Ensure that all relevant OPA, amended agreements, proposals, budgets, reports, BACS documents, and any other related or updated information are uploaded to the OPAL General Attachments section in a timely and accurate manner before closure of contract and projects.
  • Ensure Contract, project and PIP closure is carried out to a high standard and provide needful support to program managers for project closure.
  • Provides support in OPAL, as country focal person, which is Oxfam’s project management platform.
  • Support the Budget Process during the Annual COP Budget Planning and also the Year End process

Reporting to donors 40%

  • Prepare calendar tracking donor reporting deadlines and quarterly/bi-annual/annual plan submission deadlines for donors; share; and follow up with respective team members so as to ensure timely submission of reports and plans to donors.
  • Review and submit donor financial and narrative reports, ensuring consistency, accuracy, clarity and timely submission in compliance with Oxfam policies and procedures as well as donor contractual requirements, and working with programme/finance/logistics staff to improve understanding, visibility and clarity around donor contractual requirements, including facilitating donor monitoring and timely intervention.
  • Maintain documentation of communication, correspondence or agreed action point with the donor and keep the program and finance team informed of the updated requirement and changes to ensure timely compliance.
  • Coordinate with MEAL and program teams to ensure that donor reports are evidence-based, aligned with approved results frameworks and indicators, and supported by accurate data, insights, and learnings.
  • Ensure donor reports are results-oriented, effectively demonstrating outcomes, impact, and system-level change, moving beyond activity reporting to capture meaningful and sustainable Signs of Change.
  • Support key corporate reporting requirements, including the Oxfam One Program Report (OPR), Country Annual Report, reporting progress against the Country Results Framework, and other organizational reporting requirements.Maintain restricted funding information systems and records on donor contracts and income data on Oxfam’s internal contract management system (CRIMSON), box, shared drive and hard files, ensuring sign off ensuring Oxfam policies and procedures (e.g. appropriate sign-off for contracts and reports).

Donor compliance 20%

  • Facilitate and coordinate for grant orientation sessions for new awarded contracts
  • Ensure donor compliance requirements are met, enabling appropriate corrective action, such as amendments and extension requests, to be taken as necessary.
  • Accountable for providing accurate and regular information on donor rules
  • Ensures Budget Holders make necessary compliance checks in their respective project
  • Circulates donor rules.
  • Orient team members on crucial donor compliances in coordination with Contract risks management team/OGB EA and PD
  • Trains partners and Oxfam teams in donor and Oxfam rules in coordination with Contract risks management team/OGB EA and PD

Other

  • Required to adhere to Oxfam’s principles and values as well as the promotion of gender justice and women’s rights
  • Understanding of and commitment to adhere to equity, diversity, gender, child safety and staff health and wellbeing principles

Organisational Values

Equality: We believe everyone has the right to be treated fairly and to have the same rights and opportunities.

Empowerment: We acknowledge and seek to expand people’s agency over their lives and the decisions that impact them.

Solidarity: We join hands, support, and collaborate across boundaries in working towards a just and sustainable world.

Inclusiveness: We embrace diversity and difference and value the perspectives and contributions of all people and communities in their fight against poverty and injustice.

Accountability: We take responsibility for our action and inaction and hold ourselves accountable to the people we work with and for.

Courage: We speak truth to power and act with

What we are looking for:

We’re looking for a candidate who cares about Oxfam’s mission to end poverty and is personally aligned to our feminist principles and values of empowerment, accountability and inclusion in all you do.

An ideal candidate for the role will also be / have:

ESSENTIAL

Qualifications: Someone who is self-motivated, target-driven and at least three years’ experience in in contract management, donor reporting and/or donor compliances.

Education: Bachelor’s degree in finance, finance, law, management or similar

Experience:

  • Excellent organisational skills and ability to deliver to often tight deadlines; self-motivated and target-driven
  • Knowledge of donor contractual language build preferably from past experiences from institutional donors, and understanding of their rules and regulations (e.g. DFID, ECHO, OFDA, SIDA UN agencies, EU)
  • Excellent communication skills – both written and verbal (English)
  • Ability to analyse questions and collect appropriate information to respond
  • Good administrative and numerical skills associated with budgets and attention to detail
  • Highly developed interpersonal, influencing and relationship skills
  • Demonstrated organisational awareness and understanding of knowledge management
  • Ability to use Word, Excel and PowerPoint to intermediate level
  • Commitment to Oxfam’s mission and values

Essential criteria an individual needs to be able to deliver the role you can read more about here

  • Self-Awareness
  • Decisiveness
  • Relationship building

Desirable

  • Existing understanding of Oxfam’s fundraising and contract management system and procedures
  • Sound project planning skills and understanding of Programme Cycle Management in emergencies and/or development environments.
  • Blended knowledge of both financial and legal compliances in the country
  • Familiarity with one or more of Oxfam’s key operational sectors (WASH, Livelihoods and Food Security, Gender Justice, DRR)

We offer:

We offer a competitive salary and a range of additional benefits to staff including flexible working options, generous pension scheme, annual leave, additional leave allowances, company sick pay, life assurance and a range of other benefits.

From the day you join Oxfam we invite you to stretch and learn in your role. Our wide range of Learning & Development opportunities includes in-house courses, e-learning modules, on-the job learning opportunities, coaching and mentoring, and much more.

You can read more about all Oxfam has to offer here.

Flexfam:

We believe flexible working is key to building the Oxfam of the future, so we’re open to talking through the type of flexible arrangements which might work for you.

How to apply:

As part of your online application, please upload your up to date CV and Cover Letter explaining your suitability against the essential criteria in the job profile.

Our values and commitment to safeguarding

Oxfam is committed to preventing any type of unwanted behaviour at work including sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse, lack of integrity and financial misconduct; and committed to promoting the welfare of children, young people, adults and beneficiaries with whom Oxfam GB engages. Oxfam expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment through our code of conduct. We place a high priority on ensuring that only those who share and demonstrate our values are recruited to work for us.

The post holder will undertake the appropriate level of training and is responsible for ensuring that they understand and work within the safeguarding policies of the organisation.

All offers of employment will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which can include criminal records and terrorism finance checks. Oxfam GB also participates in the Inter Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme. In line with this Scheme, we will request information from job applicants’ previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment, or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms his/her understanding of these recruitment procedures.

We are committed to ensuring diversity and gender equality within our organisation and encourage applicants from diverse backgrounds to apply.

About us

Oxfam is a global community who believe poverty isn’t inevitable. It’s an injustice that can be overcome. We are shop volunteers, women’s right activists, marathon runners, aid workers, coffee farmers, street fundraisers, goat herders, policy experts, campaigners, water engineers and more. And we won’t stop until everyone can live life without poverty for good.

Oxfam GB is a member of international confederation of 21 organisations working together with partners and local communities in the areas of humanitarian, development and campaigning, in more than 90 countries.

A thriving diverse Oxfam:

It’s people power that brings about change. To play our part as a global organisation working to overcome poverty and inequality, we need equality, diversity and inclusion across our community of staff, partners and volunteers. Together, we’re committed to becoming a more diverse workforce, better able to tackle the global challenges that face our world today.

To do that:

We need to dismantle the unequal power structures that exist everywhere, this including Oxfam and the wider development and charity sectors.
We need an inclusive Oxfam where everyone can bring who they are to our work and feels celebrated for the differences they bring.
We want and need everyone, and that means we need you.

Position: Credit Analyst (CA)
Location: Lalitpur

About Us:

At Alaya, we pride ourselves on our guiding values of Care, Passion, and Oneness. We take pride in offering tailored solutions to our clients, helping them achieve their financial goals with confidence. As a member of our team, you will have the opportunity to collaborate with like-minded individuals, celebrate your unique talents, and build meaningful professional connections.

Our dedication to employee well-being and success has earned us numerous awards, including the 2023 HRD Asia 5-Star Employers of Choice Award, the 2021 Liberty Australian Brokerage of the Year Award and the Best Community Engagement Program 2024.

About The Role:

As a Credit Analyst, you will play a critical role in supporting mortgage brokers through the assessment and submission lifecycle for the Australian home loan market. This role requires strong attention to detail, a sound understanding of lender policies, and the ability to complete accurate, compliant, and timely loan assessments.

You will be responsible for reviewing client files, assessing scenarios, preparing preliminary assessments and application forms, checking lender requirements, and identifying missing documents before submission. You will also work closely with brokers, Loan Processing Specialists, lenders, and internal stakeholders to ensure smooth file progression from assessment through to post-submission and post-settlement support.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys solving complex scenarios, working with detailed information, learning lender policies, and contributing to the quality and accuracy of mortgage brokerage services.

About You:

  • You thrive in a fast-paced environment where accuracy, compliance, and strong attention to detail are valued.
  • You take responsibility for outcomes, not just tasks, and understand that even small documentation or data errors can lead to serious compliance risks.
  • You are proactive in finding solutions, asking the right questions, and contacting lenders or internal stakeholders to clarify requirements when needed.
  • You have a strong desire to learn and develop professionally, especially in credit assessment, lender policies, loan structures, and the Australian home loan market.
  • You communicate clearly and professionally with brokers, Loan Processing Specialists, and team members to ensure smooth coordination and timely file progression.
  • You are organised, dependable, and able to manage multiple priorities while maintaining quality and accuracy in your work.
  • You collaborate well with others, support team success, and are open to sharing knowledge when required.
  • If you prefer routine tasks with limited learning or are not comfortable taking ownership of accuracy and compliance, this role may not be the right fit.

Major Deliverables:

  • Assess client files once completed forms and required documents are received.
  • Contact lenders to determine client eligibility and identify suitable loan structures.
  • Prepare preliminary assessments and application forms before submission.
  • Review lender checklists, identify missing documents, and complete required loan checklists.
  • Identify and address compliance issues and inform brokers accordingly.
  • Support brokers in maintaining existing client portfolios and ensuring timely post-settlement service.
  • Follow approved processes for documentation, data security, client confidentiality, and ISO 27001:2022 requirements.
  • Support team development through knowledge sharing and guidance to new team members when required.
  • Complete ad hoc tasks, projects, and related duties as assigned.

Requirements

Apply if you have:

  • Master’s degree running or completed in Finance, Business, Management, or a related field, ACCA candidates with no more than 3 papers remaining, or semi-qualified CA candidates.
  • At least 2 years of experience in the finance sector.
  • Top-notch written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong attention to detail, especially when reviewing loan files, documents, lender checklists, and compliance requirements.
  • Problem-solving ability and a solution-focused mindset.
  • General numerical and financial calculation skills.
  • Strong planning and organisational skills.
  • Ability to prioritise tasks and handle multiple projects simultaneously.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced environment with accuracy and consistency.
  • A strong desire to learn and develop professionally, as there will be a significant learning curve.
  • Proficiency in Google Apps, including Google Drive, Docs, and Sheets.
  • Strong work ethics, accountability, and dependability.

Career Progression

The Credit Analyst role provides a strong pathway for professional growth within credit assessment, mortgage broking, and leadership functions.

With strong performance, continued learning, and demonstrated ownership, team members may progress towards roles such as:

  • Senior Credit Analyst
  • Mortgage Broker
  • Credit Team Leader or Manager

Benefits

Why should you join us?

At Alaya, we love the work we do and the colleagues we work with. We offer great growth and career advancement opportunities for our employees. While we operate in a fast-paced environment, we also value a supportive culture where people can learn, grow, and contribute meaningfully.

In this role, you will gain exposure to the Australian mortgage industry, develop strong technical knowledge in credit assessment, and play an important part in supporting brokers and clients through accurate and compliant loan assessments.

And yes, we work only 5 days a week!

What we offer:

Besides the list of benefits that the Labour Law mandates, we also offer:

  • Salary + Social Security Fund (SSF)
  • 5-day work week, Monday to Friday
  • Exclusive paid leaves
  • Conducive and fun working environment
  • Festival, profit, and book reading bonus
  • Team building activities and social events
  • Accidental and medical insurance coverage
  • International working environment exposure
  • Continuous learning and development opportunities

Plus, take advantage of our Customer Referral program to earn rewards by recommending our services to friends and relatives in Australia.

Our office is open, so if you’re selected, we’d be happy to work with you in person!

You also acknowledge and consent that your application may be reviewed and processed with the support of AI tools, and that certain stages of the recruitment process may include recorded transcriptions that may be processed through AI to support fair, accurate, and efficient recruitment decisions. Your data will be stored securely and will only be accessible to authorised personnel.

Ready to Apply?

If you’re looking for a role where your attention to detail, problem-solving ability, and willingness to learn can make a real impact, we’d love to hear from you.

Join us and be part of a team that values growth, collaboration, accuracy, and excellence.

Position: Officer, Information Technology

Guided by the remarkable legacy of its co-founder, Helen Keller, Helen Keller Intl partners with communities striving to overcome longstanding cycles of poverty. By delivering the essential building blocks of good health, sound nutrition, and clear vision, we help millions of people create lasting change in their own lives. Working in 20 countries – across Africa, Asia, Europe, and the United States – and together with a global community of supporters, we ensure every person has the opportunity – as Helen did – to reach their true potential.

Brief Background: Helen Keller’s Nepal country office relies on a stable, secure information systems environment to support programs delivered across a range of locations, including districts with significant infrastructure challenges. This role ensures that staff have the technology support, network connectivity, and security practices they need to do their work effectively, while working closely with regional and global Information Systems colleagues to uphold organizational standards.

Purpose or Scope of work

The Officer, Information Technology oversees the country office’s information systems, working with regional and global colleagues to ensure network administration, hardware and application management, security, and user support are properly managed. The role requires a broad set of technical, planning, problem-solving, and hands-on support skills, along with the ability to work effectively in low-resource settings that present real infrastructure challenges. Above all, this position supports Helen Keller’s mission by keeping the technology that underpins our programs secure, reliable, and accessible, working collaboratively across a multicultural environment.

Management/ Functional Relationships

This role reports to the Senior Manager, Operations, with a dotted-line relationship to the Senior Manager, Information Technology. It works closely with regional and global Information Systems colleagues and collaborates internally with all Nepal-based staff. Externally, the role coordinates with partner organizations on network connectivity, as needed.

Application Deadline: August 30, 2026

Key Responsibilities/ Specific Tasks

  • Technical/Programmatic: Maintain and support information system components across Helen Keller’s Nepal offices, including hardware, applications, and network infrastructure, in line with global information systems standards.
  • Technical/Programmatic: Apply security patches and support security awareness initiatives to protect information systems and prevent security incidents.
  • Operations/Coordination: Manage information technology service requests through Helen Keller’s Fresh Service platform and coordinate escalations with regional technical support teams.
  • Operations/Coordination: Coordinate procurement and management of information technology assets across the country office.
  • External Engagement: Coordinate network connectivity support with partner organizations, as needed.

Other Duties

This job announcement is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive list of activities, duties or responsibilities for the position. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice. All positions are required to perform any additional tasks assigned by the supervisor.

Skills & Experience

Technical & Leadership Competencies

  • Strong knowledge of technical management, information analysis, and computer hardware and software systems.
  • Hands-on experience with network installation, management, and data center governance.

Operational & Functional Skills

  • Excellent written and spoken Nepali and English language skills.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint, and the ability to work independently in a dynamic, low-resource environment.

Education & Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, information technology, engineering, or a related field required; or associate/technical diploma with 4+ years of directly related experience.
  • 3–4 years of relevant professional experience in an Information Technology support role, with a background in computer science, information technology, engineering, or a related discipline.

Working Conditions/ Travel

  • Travel expectations: Occasional travel to district offices within Nepal to support network connectivity and hardware needs.
  • Work environment: Office-based role in a low-resource setting that requires adaptability and hands-on problem-solving.
  • Safeguarding responsibilities: Adherence to Helen Keller’s Code of Conduct and safeguarding policies.
  • Language requirements: Fluency in Nepali and English, written and spoken.

Expectations

Fairness, Belonging and Zero Tolerance to Abuse

As a member of the Helen Keller Family, each employee is expected to:

  • Help to develop and maintain an environment that welcomes and develops a multi-cultural workforce with varied lived experiences and identities.
  • Foster a work environment where everyone feels valued and included.
  • Support employees’ evaluation and promotion processes based on skills and performance.
  • Promote a safe, secure, and respectful environment for all members of Helen Keller family, stakeholders in general, and particularly for the communities we serve.
  • Follow Helen Keller Code of Conduct helping to prevent any type of abuse including workplace harassment, sexual abuse and exploitation, and trafficking in persons.
  • Adhere to the Organizational Core Values, which include courage, compassion, integrity and rigor.

To Apply

Qualified candidates should submit a cover letter and resume to Nepal.Recruitment@hki.org. Applications will be accepted until August 30, 2026. Click here to view the detailed Job Description.

Organization Description

The Why: NEPAL aspires to graduate from least developing country to a lower middle-income country by 2026. However, the development community’s excessive focus today on socio-political empowerment has not yielded the desired economic transformation. In reaching the 2026 national target, shall we wait for institutions of power to become accountability productive or shall we bolster innovations of people to bring inclusive prosperity? How do we strengthen grassroots-government collaboration in shaping an equal and enterprising future?

The How: DAAYITWA, with a focus on economic empowerment, envisions an enterprising Nepal where every youth has opportunities for a prosperous future. Daayitwa is a part of the Daayitwa Abhiyaan which consists of four organizations: Daayitwa, Governance Lab, Nepal Leadership Academy based in Nepal and Nepal Rising (Daayitwa-US) based in the U.S. Inspired by shared values of innovation, collaboration, and service, it promotes the socio- economic development of Nepal. The movement fosters inclusive and equitable economic growth by accelerating grassroots innovations, strengthening government institutions, and revitalizing a virtuous cycle of democracy and development through grassroots-government collaboration.

Our Focus Areas:

1. Promote enterprise-led employment creation

2. Design evidence-based policies for improved decision-making

3. Build state capability for effective policy implementation

4. Foster stakeholder collaboration for governance innovations

Daayitwa runs several programs and initiatives aimed at our focus area.

Job Description

The What: We are looking for a full-time Research Associate who will (a) work closely with a research team based at top international universities to develop study protocols (b) collaborate with on-ground policy partners to execute the study and collect monitoring data; and (c) collect, clean and analyse data from large-scale field surveys in our study sample. The Research Associate will be based in Kathmandu, with occasional travel to study field sites. This position requires a self-starting candidate, who enjoys working on cutting edge research that informs policy. The candidate will have a unique opportunity to drive efforts to ensure that government policy priorities inform research agenda and vice versa. The candidate will also conduct in-depth interviews and scoping activities, engage with government stakeholders, manage field activities and coordinate field staff for the execution of primary data collection activities. She/he will support high-quality cleaning and rigorous analysis of both primary and secondary data, and work with a team of leading economists and public policy experts from top universities across the world and the Inclusion Economics India Centre. It is an excellent opportunity for someone interested in a career in academic research to work closely with a Principal Investigator team that includes Rohini Pande (Yale University) Maulik Jagnani (Tufts University), and George Taylor (UC Berkeley).

The Project:

Urban and peri-urban flooding imposes severe and growing economic costs across South Asia, with the burden falling disproportionately on the informal firms that form the backbone of local economies. Kathmandu’s peri-urban and urban economy is built on a dense population of informal firms whose financial fragility makes flood disruption acutely damaging and adaptation especially difficult; evidence from similar settings shows that firms systematically underinvest in protection even when adaptation would be cost-effective, and the evidence base on why — and what would shift their behaviour — remains thin. This proposal outlines a randomised study testing whether timely flood forecast information allows formal and informal firms in Kathmandu to take anticipatory measures to prevent flood damages, generating evidence to support climate-resilient economic growth in Nepal.

The central question is whether information constraints are the binding obstacle to adaptation among Kathmandu’s peri-urban formal and informal firms. Treatment firms receive timely forecast dissemination, and the study measures outcomes including days of business closure, inventory losses, worker layoffs, and changes in procurement and sales patterns, as well as relevant outcomes for neighbouring firms, connected suppliers, workers, and consumers.

Responsibilities:

In collaboration with the research and senior project teams, the Research Associate will be required to:

  • Conduct data cleaning and analysis of multiple primary and secondary data sources.
  •  Seek out and collect administrative data from partners and government agencies.
  • Assist in the design and field-testing of scoping and survey instruments.
  • Support the day-to-day implementation of field-based research including scoping, surveying,field staff recruitment, training & supervision.
  • Support with writing research outputs such as policy briefs, research articles, etc.
  •  Review and report on academic literature of requested topics in support of concept notes, policy briefs and research projects.
  • Manage day-to-day relationships with officials at all three spheres of government, policy and program partners in academia, civil society etc., as requested.
  • Others, as required

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree with experience in data-based research, preferably in economics, political economy, political science, or a related field.
  •  Strong interest in public policy and economic development in low-income countries.
  •  Excellent oral and written communication skills in Nepali and English languages.
  •  Proficiency in Stata and/or other statistical tools and the Microsoft Office suite.
  • Mature, self-directed individual with ability to balance multiple tasks and prioritize effectively to meet deadlines in a fast-paced working environment.
  • Ability and willingness to travel regularly and frequently to other parts of the country.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with data based research in Stata and/or other statistical tools is highly desired.
  • Strong interpersonal skills and demonstrated ability to engage with partners at various levels.
  • Additional local language skills (apart from English and Nepali).
  •  Field experience and administering surveys will be an added advantage.
  • Prior experience with external stakeholder engagement such as government, donors, development agencies, and/or political parties.

What we offer

  • A dynamic and engaging environment within our office in Kathmandu, with our India based partner, and with internationally acclaimed researchers.
  •  A competitive salary by local standards.
  •  Regular travel within Nepal.

Additional information

Posiiton: Disaster Risk Management Specialist-Heat Lead
Location: Kathmandu with frequent travel to working areas

About Mercy Corps

Mercy Corps is a leading global organization powered by the belief that a better world is possible. In disaster, in hardship, in more than 40 countries around the world, we partner to put bold solutions into action – helping people triumph over adversity and build stronger communities from within. Now, and for the future. Mercy Corps has been operating in Nepal since 2005, implementing programs in food security, agriculture, market development, financial services, youth engagement, climate change adaptation and disaster risk reduction. We take a systems-based approach in our programming, with the aim of improving the lives and potential of vulnerable individuals and communities across Nepal.

Program/Department Summary

The Zurich Climate Resilience Alliance (ZCRA) is an alliance of nine organizations including international NGOs, private sector, and academic organizations, who have come together with the support of the Zurich Foundation to drive better policy and practice to reduce the negative impact of floods on peoples’ and communities’ ability to thrive.

The Alliance is implementing a 12-year vision through 2025. The current phase (phase 3, 2024-2027) represents the first cycle of this long-term vision. Previously, the Alliance completed its first phase in 2018, and its second phase in December 2023 and third phase will run till Dec 2027. During this time, The Alliance works together to achieve 12-year vision by implementing solutions, promoting good practice, influencing policy and facilitating systemic change. In Nepal, the Alliance is comprised of Mercy Corps and Practical Action, working together on joint outcomes aiming at:

  • Building ex-ante resilience of communities at risk of flood and heat impacts across Nepal
  • Improving early warning and early action in advance of probable hazards
  • Enabling people who experience livelihoods losses due to floods and heat to recover quickly through compensation and/or insurance

General Position Summary

The Disaster Risk Management Specialist – Heat Lead will serve as Mercy Corps’ technical lead on heat resilience, providing technical expertise and coordination to strengthen the management of extreme heat risks across programmes and partnerships in Nepal. The position will lead the design, implementation, and quality assurance of heat resilience interventions and support the integration of heat risk management into disaster risk reduction, climate change adaptation, health, urban planning, livelihoods, and resilience programming. Working closely with government agencies, technical institutions, development partners, academia, the private sector, and communities, the Heat Lead will strengthen heat governance, policy, planning, early warning systems, and sustainable financing while promoting gender equality, disability inclusion, and locally led approaches. The role will also lead research, knowledge management, capacity strengthening, technical advocacy, and resource mobilization to enhance evidence-based programming and support the scale-up of heat resilience initiatives in Nepal. While heat resilience will be the primary technical focus of the position, the Specialist will also provide technical support to broader disaster risk management programming, including flood and wildfire resilience initiatives, ensuring integrated multi-hazard approaches across Mercy Corps’ resilience portfolio.

As gender and social inclusion (GESI), governance and environmental compliance are cross-cutting and core components of all MC programs and is required to own these components to ensure GESI sensitivity and integration, governance practices and environmental compliance are integrated into the program activities.

Essential Job Responsibilities

The specific duties and responsibilities of the Disaster Risk Management Specialist -Heat Lead include, but are not limited to, the following:

1. Technical Leadership, Thought Leadership and Program Development (25%)

  • Serve as Mercy Corps’ technical focal point on heat resilience and provide strategic leadership across program components.
  • Provide thought leadership on heat resilience by promoting innovative approaches, generating evidence, influencing national discourse, and positioning Mercy Corps as a leading technical partner on heat risk management in Nepal.
  • Lead the design, implementation, and quality assurance of heat resilience interventions, ensuring alignment with national priorities and global good practices.
  • Provide technical guidance on integrating heat risk management and GESI considerations into DRR, climate adaptation, health, urban planning, livelihoods, and resilience programming to ensure inclusive and equitable outcomes.
  • Develop technical tools, training packages, guidance notes, methodologies, and standards on heat to support program implementation.
  • Identify emerging trends, best practices and opportunities for innovation and scaling of heat resilience interventions through research, technology, partnerships, and adaptive programming.
  • Lead and contribute to technical publications, policy briefs, conference presentations, webinars, and knowledge-sharing events to advance learning and influence policy and practice on heat resilience.
  • While leading Mercy Corps’ heat resilience portfolio, provide technical support to flood, wildfire, and other multi-hazard disaster risk management initiatives, promoting integrated and risk-informed approaches across programs.

2. Heat Governance, Policy and Systems Strengthening (25%)

  • Support federal, provincial and local governments to strengthen institutional mechanisms for heat governance.
  • Lead technical support for the development and implementation of Heat Action Plans (HAPs), heat governance strategies, technical guidelines, and standard operating procedures.
  • Strengthen integration of heat risk management into disaster management, climate adaptation, health, urban development, and sectoral plans.
  • Support the development and strengthening of heat early warning systems, impact-based forecasting, and preparedness protocols in collaboration with technical agencies.
  • Support the integration of heat priorities into government planning, budgeting, budget advocacy, expenditure tracking, and climate finance mechanisms to strengthen sustainable investment in heat resilience.
  • Support community empowerment on heat resilience through awareness campaigns, risk communication, behaviour change initiatives, and community engagement, ensuring vulnerable groups have the knowledge and capacity to prepare for, respond to, and adapt to extreme heat.
  • Promote the integration of GESI considerations into heat governance, policies, plans, and institutional mechanisms to ensure that the needs and priorities of women, children, older persons, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups are addressed.
  • Provide technical support for heat-responsive planning, budget advocacy, and expenditure tracking at federal, provincial, and local levels to strengthen investment and accountability for heat resilience.
  • Coordinate and strengthen partnerships with government institutions, including Ministry of Federal Affairs and General Administration, National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, Department of Hydrology and Meteorology, the Ministry of Health, provincial governments, development partners, academia, and the private sector.
  • Support the establishment and strengthening of multi-stakeholder coordination platforms and communities of practice to promote collaboration, knowledge exchange, and coordinated action on heat resilience.
  • While leading heat resilience initiatives, provide technical support to the integration of flood, wildfire, and other priority hazards into government policies, plans, and coordination mechanisms to strengthen multi-hazard disaster risk management.

3. Program Implementation, Capacity Strengthening and Partnership (25%)

  • Lead heat hotspot mapping, vulnerability assessments, heat studies and research to inform program design and policy.
  • Provide technical oversight for the implementation of Heat Action Plans and community-based heat resilience interventions, ensuring they are gender-responsive, disability-inclusive, and accessible to vulnerable populations.
  • Support implementation of heat mitigation measures including cooling centres, nature-based solutions, drinking water facilities, heat-resilient infrastructure, and public awareness initiatives etc. and ensure effective implementation in accordance with program standards and global best practices.
  • Support implementation of heat resilience interventions that strengthen the resilience of local enterprises, workers, and markets to extreme heat.
  • Build the capacity of government officials, municipalities, health workers, schools, community disaster management committees, media, and partner organizations on inclusive heat risk management, ensuring meaningful participation and leadership of women, persons with disabilities, older persons, and other vulnerable groups.
  • Foster partnerships with research institutions, academia, private sector actors, and technical organizations to promote innovation and collaboration.
  • Lead the planning, coordination, and facilitation of heat resilience workshops, consultations, and technical dialogues at federal, provincial, and local levels.
  • Provide technical support to the design, implementation, and quality assurance of flood, wildfire, and other multi-hazard resilience interventions, as required, ensuring alignment with program standards and integrated disaster risk management approaches.

4. Knowledge Management, Monitoring and Resource Mobilization (20%)

  • Lead research, documentation of program learning, evidence, case studies, technical reports, and knowledge products.
  • Monitor implementation progress, analyse program performance, and support adaptive management.
  • Develop and track program indicators related to heat resilience and contribute to monitoring, evaluation, accountability, and learning (MEAL) processes.
  • Prepare technical inputs for donor reports, presentations, policy briefs, and communication products.
  • Represent Mercy Corps in national and international technical working groups, forums, and coordination platforms related to heat and climate resilience.
  • Contribute to proposal development, technical design, and resource mobilization efforts to expand Mercy Corps’ heat resilience portfolio.
  • Promote cross-learning and knowledge sharing across heat, flood, wildfire, and other disaster risk management programs to strengthen integrated multi-hazard resilience programming.

Others

Conduct himself/herself both professionally and personally in such a manner as to bring credit to Mercy Corps and to not jeopardize its humanitarian mission.
Mercy Corps as a humanitarian agency is expected to response as and when crisis and humanitarian situation engulfs. As an MC employee, all staff are expected to be part of humanitarian and emergency response in addition to their regular roles and responsibilities in such situations.
Other duties as assigned by the Country Director.

Security

Proactively ensure that team members operate in a secure environment and are aware of policies.

Accountability to Beneficiaries

  • Mercy Corps team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our beneficiaries and to international standards guiding international relief and development work, while actively engaging beneficiary communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring, and evaluation of our field projects.
  • Team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner and respect local laws, customs and MC’s policies, procedures, and values always and in all in-country venues.

Supervisory Responsibility: N/A

  • Reports Directly to: CRC Program Manager
  • Works Closely with: Province Coordinator(s), Senior Advocacy and Influencing Officer, Private Sector Engagement Specialist, Implementing Partners, Mercy Corps’ cross functional departments, other programs, ZCRA Alliance III partners – Practical Action etc.

Knowledge and Experience

  • Master’s degree in Disaster Risk Management, Climate Change, Environmental Science, Urban Planning, Engineering, Geography, or a related field.
  • At least 6 years of experience in disaster risk reduction (DRR), climate change adaptation, resilience, or related fields, including at least 3 years of specific experience in heat resilience or extreme heat programming.
  • Demonstrated experience in developing and implementing Heat Action Plans, heat resilience strategies, or related policies and programs.
  • Strong knowledge and experience of heat risk assessment, vulnerability analysis, early warning systems, impact-based forecasting, and climate data interpretation.
  • Proven experience in conducting research, synthesizing technical evidence, and translating research findings into practical recommendations, policies, and programs design.
  • Demonstrated experience in developing high-quality knowledge products, including technical reports, policy briefs, guidance notes, case studies, training materials, and communication products.
  • Experience in knowledge management, documentation of lessons learned, evidence generation, and facilitating learning and knowledge-sharing processes.
  • Strong experience working with federal, provincial, and local government institutions, technical agencies, and development partners.
  • Strong facilitation, stakeholder engagement, partnership development, and capacity-building skills.
  • Excellent analytical, coordination, project management, and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent report writing, technical writing, and verbal communication skills in both English and Nepali.
  • Experience integrating GESI principles into disaster risk reduction, climate adaptation, or resilience programming.
  • Experience working with international NGOs, bilateral or multilateral donors, or donor-funded program.

Accountability to Participants and Stakeholders

Mercy Corps team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our program participants, community partners, other stakeholders, and to international standards guiding international relief and development work. We are committed to actively engaging communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring and evaluation of our field projects.

Success Factors

A successful candidate will have the ability to live and work closely with a diverse team of individuals in a highly intense and fluid work and security environment with a capacity to spark innovative approaches to programming and inspire groups to collaborate closely to implement high-quality programs. They will have a proven ability to learn quickly, take initiative, and be accountable for results, with an ability and willingness to remain mobile for short-term and/or long-term as necessary within the region, based on programmatic needs. An ability to work independently and as part of a team, with curiosity about and sensitivity to new cultures, a desire and ability to learn and grow, both personally and professionally, and a great sense of humor.

The most successful Mercy Corps team members have a strong commitment to teamwork and accountability, thrive in evolving and changing environments and make effective written and verbal communication a priority in all situations. Mercy Corps Team members represent the agency both during and outside of work hours when deployed in a field posting or on a visit/short-term assignment to a field posting. Team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner and respect local laws, customs and MC’s policies, procedures, and values at all times and in all in-country venues.

Living Conditions / Environmental Conditions

The position is based in Kathmandu, and it requires up to 50% travel to support country programs.

Ongoing Learning

In support of our belief that learning organizations are more effective, efficient and relevant to the communities we serve, we empower all team members to dedicate 5% of their time to learning activities that further their personal and/or professional growth and development.

Diversity, Equity & Inclusion

Achieving our mission begins with how we build our team and work together. Through our commitment to enriching our organization with people of different origins, beliefs, backgrounds, and ways of thinking, we are better able to leverage the collective power of our teams and solve the world’s most complex challenges. We strive for a culture of trust and respect, where everyone contributes their perspectives and authentic selves, reaches their potential as individuals and teams, and collaborates to do the best work of their lives.

We recognize that diversity and inclusion is a journey, and we are committed to learning, listening and evolving to become more diverse, equitable and inclusive than we are today.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Mercy Corps is an equal opportunity employer that does not tolerate discrimination on any basis. We actively seek out diverse backgrounds, perspectives, and skills so that we can be collectively stronger and have sustained global impact.

We are committed to providing an environment of respect and psychological safety where equal employment opportunities are available to all. We do not engage in or tolerate discrimination on the basis of race, color, gender identity, gender expression, religion, age, sexual orientation, national or ethnic origin, disability (including HIV/AIDS status), marital status, military veteran status or any other protected group in the locations where we work.

Safeguarding & Ethics

Mercy Corps is committed to ensuring that all individuals we come into contact with through our work, whether team members, community members, program participants or others, are treated with respect and dignity. We are committed to the core principles regarding prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse laid out by the UN Secretary General and IASC and have signed on to The Misconduct Disclosure Scheme We will not tolerate child abuse, sexual exploitation, abuse, or harassment by or of our team members. As part of our commitment to a safe and inclusive work environment, team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner, respect local laws and customs, and to adhere to Mercy Corps Code of Conduct Policies and values at all times. Team members must complete mandatory Code of Conduct eLearning courses upon hire and annually.

As an applicant, if you witness or experience any form of sexual misconduct during the recruitment process, please report this to Mercy Corps Integrity Hotline (integrityhotline@mercycorps.org).

S/He will provide technical guidance to DCA, team and partners, as well as ensure that activities are implemented timely and to a high standard while ensuring linkages with deliverables under Early Warning System – Early Adaptation, inclusion, localization and Shock Responsive Social Protection.
