  • Provide technical leadership on all adaptation and specific resilience activities
  • Supervise the design and implementation of locally-led adaptation interventions
  • Co-develop and deliver training with support from partner’s Adaptation Coordinator to CBOs and local governments on climate adaptation and its strategies.
  • Build capacity of CBOs and LG’s of RAIN in risk-informed planning, climate-smart practices, and leveraging fiscal resources for adaptation.
  • Lead the implementation of adaptation and specific resilience activities including supervising and closely collaborating with partner staff for this component; guiding and supervising Adaptation Coordinators as well as collaborating with LG Officers based at the local government level.
  • Together with DCA Climate Action Advisor and implementing partners, provide capacity building to DCA staff, consortium partners, CBOs and relevant stakeholders on adaptation and components of resilience and develop high-quality training materials and curricula.
  • Contribute to the Resilience Measurement Framework together with RAIN MEAL Lead and EWS EA Lead.
  • Collaborate closely with the Climate Action Advisor, Consortium Manager and DCA’s Global Advisers in developing knowledge products, and internal, governmental and donor reports, together with reporting to other stakeholders/groups (technical working group, clusters).
  • Represent DCA and RAIN project professionally with external stakeholders, including government, non-governmental agencies and donors especially in Madhesh and Lumbini, and especially to stakeholders in adaptation and resilience
  • Together with MEAL lead and Communication & Advocacy Manager, engage in project-learning-based positioning and advocacy, development of learning papers and selection of advocacy points for SARATHI, as per Country Strategy

Qualification, Skill and Knowledge:

  • Master’s degree in civil engineering, climate change, natural resource management, disaster risk management, environment science or relevant field, with 5 years of work experience with an I/NGO or development organization in the area of climate adaptation and resilience.
  • Strong track record in designing and leading climate adaptation and resilience initiatives in Nepal, engagement with regional and global adaptation and resilience programmes is an advantage.
  • Expert knowledge and experience in watershed management and application of nature-based solutions in river basin management and its linkages with ecosystem services
  • Experience working with diverse stakeholders in climate change, DRRM and AA sector, especially with local, district, provincial and federal level actors.
  • Commitment to systems strengthening approaches, proven track record in adaptive management and facilitation approach for adaptation and resilience in Nepal.
  • Experience in field-based understanding of vulnerabilities, exposure and risk in the multi-hazard context of Nepal.
  • Experience in watershed management and application of nature-based solutions in river basin management and its linkages with ecosystem services
  • Construction experience (bioengineering designs, safe shelter construction, and other mitigation efforts) is an advantage.
  • Sound knowledge of existing climate resilience frameworks.
  • Demonstrated experience in coordinating diverse teams and maintaining strong relationships with the project team, partners and local stakeholders.
  • Outstanding communications and networking skills; with a strong command of Nepali and English languages- written and spoken.

Posiiton: ECA & CCA Coordinator
Location: Lalitpur

The ECA & CCA Coordinator is responsible for planning, coordinating, implementing, monitoring, and evaluating all Extra Curricular Activities and Co-Curricular Activities of United Academy and United College. The position is responsible for ensuring that ECA and CCA programs are well planned, student focused, safe, financially responsible, and aligned with the institution’s academic and student development objectives.

Key Result Areas and Responsibilities

1. Annual Planning and Activity Coordination

  • Develop and maintain the annual ECA and CCA calendar in consultation with the Academic Head and Principal.
  • Plan a balanced range of academic, sports, cultural, artistic, recreational, leadership, and skill based activities.
  • Coordinate with relevant departments, teachers, instructors, student representatives, and external organizations for the successful implementation of activities.
  • Ensure that all planned activities are conducted smoothly and within the approved schedule.
  • Review the ECA and CCA calendar periodically and recommend necessary changes based on institutional requirements and student interests.
  • Develop activity plans, timelines, manpower requirements, logistical arrangements, and other requirements for each major activity.

2. Student Engagement and Participation

  • Promote active student participation in ECA and CCA activities.
  • Identify students’ talents, interests, skills, and areas of potential through participation in various activities.
  • Encourage wider participation by identifying barriers to student participation and developing appropriate initiatives to address them.
  • Coordinate and provide guidance to student clubs, committees, teams, and activity groups.
  • Maintain participation records for each activity and monitor participation trends.
  • Develop strategies to increase student participation in ECA and CCA programs.
  • Encourage students to participate in internal and inter level competitions, exhibitions, performances, tournaments, and other events.

3. Budget and Resource Management

  • Prepare the annual and activity specific budget requirements for ECA and CCA programs.
  • Obtain prior approval for budgets and expenditures before implementing activities.
  • Coordinate with Procurement, Store, Finance, and other relevant departments for the timely availability of required resources.
  • Ensure effective and economical utilization of the approved budget and resources.
  • Maintain proper records of expenditure and supporting documents for each activity.
  • Identify opportunities to maximize the impact of activities while maintaining cost effectiveness.

4. Manpower and Logistics Coordination

  • Assess and plan the manpower requirement for each ECA and CCA activity.
  • Coordinate with teachers, instructors, support staff, volunteers, security personnel, transport teams, and other relevant personnel as required.
  • Ensure appropriate allocation of responsibilities before and during each activity.
  • Coordinate venue arrangements, equipment, materials, transportation, accommodation, refreshments, and other logistical requirements where applicable.
  • Ensure that all activities are adequately staffed and operationally prepared.

5. External Resource Person and Guest Coordination

  • Establish and maintain professional relationships with sports persons, artists, trainers, coaches, industry professionals, guest lecturers, and other relevant external resource persons.
  • Coordinate with external resource persons regarding their availability, participation, requirements, and schedules.
  • Maintain an updated record of visiting resource persons, guest lecturers, trainers, coaches, and other external contributors.
  • Prepare reports and maintain supporting documentation for activities involving external resource persons.
  • Explore opportunities to introduce new experts and professionals who can add value to student development programs.

6. Safety, Compliance and Risk Management

  • Ensure that appropriate safety measures are implemented for all ECA and CCA activities.
  • Conduct basic risk assessment and identify potential safety concerns before activities are conducted.
  • Coordinate with relevant personnel to address identified safety risks.
  • Ensure that activities comply with the policies, procedures, rules, and standards of United Academy College.
  • Ensure appropriate supervision of students during activities, events, tours, field trips, competitions, and other programs.
  • Immediately report any significant safety, disciplinary, or operational concern to the Academic Head or Principal.

7. Event and Competition Management

  • Plan and coordinate ECA and CCA events, competitions, exhibitions, showcases, tournaments, performances, and other student activities.
  • Ensure smooth coordination of schedules, venues, participants, judges, coaches, guests, equipment, and other requirements.
  • Coordinate internal and interlevel competitions and encourage increased student participation.
  • Maintain records of participation, results, achievements, awards, and recognitions.
  • Facilitate appropriate recognition and celebration of students’ achievements.
  • Conduct post event reviews to identify strengths, challenges, and areas for improvement.

8. Educational Tours and Field Trips

  • Coordinate the planning and execution of educational tours, field visits, excursions, and other off campus student activities.
  • Maintain proper records of educational tours and field trips, including participants, destination, dates, responsible personnel, and relevant reports.
  • Coordinate with relevant departments and service providers for logistical arrangements.
  • Ensure appropriate student supervision, safety, documentation, and compliance with institutional requirements.

9. Communication and Promotion

  • Communicate ECA and CCA schedules, requirements, notices, and updates to students, teachers, staff, and parents where applicable.
  • Promote ECA and CCA programs to encourage student participation.
  • Coordinate with the Brand, Engagement, Communication, and relevant teams for appropriate promotion and documentation of activities.
  • Ensure timely communication of activity related information to all concerned stakeholders.
  • Support the development of appropriate promotional and informational materials for major ECA and CCA activities.

10. Monitoring, Evaluation and Reporting

  • Monitor the implementation and effectiveness of ECA and CCA activities.
  • Collect feedback from students, teachers, parents, and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Analyse participation levels, student satisfaction, achievements, and outcomes of activities.
  • Identify activities with low participation and recommend strategies to improve engagement.
  • Prepare a report for each major ECA and CCA activity.
  • Prepare periodic consolidated reports covering activities conducted, participation, achievements, expenditure, challenges, and recommendations.
  • Review the effectiveness of ECA and CCA programs and recommend improvements for future activities.

11. Documentation and Record Keeping

  • Maintain accurate and updated records of all ECA and CCA activities.
  • Maintain records of student participation, competitions, achievements, awards, guest lecturers, resource persons, educational tours, field trips, and major events.
  • Maintain activity plans, approved budgets, reports, attendance records, photographs, certificates, results, feedback, and other supporting documents.
  • Ensure that ECA and CCA records are systematically maintained and readily available when required.
  • Maintain a database of student participation and achievements for institutional reference.

12. Continuous Improvement

  • Develop new ideas and initiatives to make ECA and CCA activities more effective and engaging.
  • Identify emerging interests and opportunities in sports, arts, culture, technology, leadership, communication, and other areas relevant to student development.
  • Benchmark suitable activities and practices from other educational institutions where appropriate.
  • Recommend new activities based on student feedback, participation trends, institutional priorities, and available resources.
  • Continuously review existing activities and recommend discontinuation, modification, or expansion based on their effectiveness.

Expected Deliverables

The position holder shall be responsible for ensuring the following key deliverables:

  • Annual ECA and CCA Calendar
  • Activity wise plans and schedules
  • Activity wise budget proposals and approvals
  • Manpower and logistics plans
  • Student participation records
  • Guest lecturer and external resource person records
  • Educational tour and field trip records
  • Activity reports and supporting documentation
  • Student feedback and satisfaction analysis
  • Participation and achievement analysis
  • Periodic ECA and CCA performance reports
  • Recommendations for improvement and development of ECA and CCA programs

JOB SPECIFICATION

Educational Qualification

  • Bachelor’s degree in Management, Education, Sports Management, Event Management, or a relevant discipline. A Master’s degree will be an advantage.

Professional Experience

  • Minimum 2 to 3 years of relevant experience in ECA/CCA coordination, student activities, event management, sports, education, or a similar role, preferably within an educational institution.

Technical Competencies

  • Good knowledge of ECA and CCA planning and implementation.
  • Good event planning and coordination skills.
  • Ability to prepare activity plans, budgets, schedules, and reports.
  • Good knowledge of student engagement and activity management.
  • Basic knowledge of safety and risk management for student activities.
  • Proficiency in MS Office and Google Workspace.
  • Ability to maintain systematic records and documentation.

Core Competencies

  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Student engagement and relationship management.
  • Planning and organizational ability.
  • Coordination and teamwork.
  • Problem solving and decision making.
  • Time management and multitasking.
  • Creativity and initiative.
  • Accountability and result orientation.

Preferred Attributes

  • Passion for student development and extracurricular activities.
  • Interest or experience in sports, arts, culture, music, or other student activities.
  • Ability to work with students of diverse interests and abilities.
  • Ability to coordinate with teachers, parents, external resource persons, and service providers.
  • Willingness to work beyond regular hours during events, competitions, tours, and special programs when required.

Personal Attributes

  • The position holder should demonstrate professionalism, discipline, patience, adaptability, enthusiasm, integrity, and a positive attitude toward students and colleagues.

Position: Project Coordinator (Policy Advocacy)

NEEDS Nepal is a non-profit, non-governmental social organization that has been actively working in the social sector for the past 27 years. The organization was established in 1999 as a youth group and has since then engaged in various social transformation, good governance, and development initiatives. NEEDS Nepal is registered with the Government of Nepal. It has partnered with numerous governments, I/NOGs, and bilateral agencies to implement programs that focus on empowerment, socio-economic development, safe shelter and social transformation for marginalized and vulnerable communities such as children, women, youths, persons with disabilities, Dalits, Janajati and other marginalized groups. NEEDS Nepal has four working themes identified through the organizational strategy plan 2024-2028: Social Justice and Rights, Climate & Disaster Resilient Action, Dignified Migration & Livelihood, and Organizational Development.

Project Brief

NEEDS Nepal, in partnership with Habitat for Humanity Nepal, is implementing the Surakshit Awash Program (SASWIN, SAFER and SABAL projects) in Kanchanpur district, Sudurpashchim province Nepal. The project aims to strengthen the resilience of vulnerable communities by promoting safe housing, disaster risk reduction (DRR), climate resilience, and inclusive community development. The SASWIN project focuses on strengthening policy and legal frameworks, enhancing institutional capacity, promoting evidence-based advocacy, and facilitating collaboration among provincial and local governments to improve access to land and housing rights. The project is being implemented in Bedkot Municipality and Shuklaphanta Municipality of Kanchanpur District. In this context, NEEDS Nepal has announced a vacancy notice for the position of Project Coordinator (Policy Advocacy). The detailed job description can be accessed through the link.

https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1KJGMPB2KY3Bfy9Ww8p_slJQyrwfry0ol?usp=drive_link

Safeguarding & PSEA

NEEDS Nepal has a zero-tolerance policy and approach to any abuse, sexual harassment, or exploitation of a vulnerable adult or child by any of our staff, volunteers, consultants, and suppliers. All individuals and institutions have committed to respecting the core principles regarding the prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse laid out by the organization’s safeguarding policy, Zero Tolerance Policy, PSEA & code of conduct that is associated with the organization.

NEEDS Nepal expects all the staff to share this commitment through Safeguarding, PSEA Policy, and Code of Conduct. All staff must be committed to ensuring that all individuals we come into contact with through our work, whether team members, community members, program participants, or others, are treated with respect and dignity.

How to apply

Qualified & eligible national citizens are highly encouraged to apply with their updated CV along with a motivation letter & expected salary in gross per month to the following email address, hr@needsnepal.org.np by 17th August 2026.

Women, ethnic minorities, and local applicants are highly encouraged to apply. No telephone calls will be entertained, and this automatically disqualifies in the recruitment process.

NEEDS Nepal will reserve all rights to make the final decision. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for the further recruitment process. The remuneration and other benefits package shall be as per NEEDS Nepal HRM policy & guidelines.

ABOUT WFP

The World Food Programme is the world’s largest humanitarian organization saving lives in emergencies and using food assistance to build a pathway to peace, stability and prosperity, for people recovering from conflict, disasters and the impact of climate change.

At WFP, people are at the heart of everything we do and the vision of the future WFP workforce is one of diverse, committed, skilled, and high performing teams, selected on merit, operating in a healthy and inclusive work environment, living WFP’s values (Integrity, Collaboration, Commitment, Humanity, and Inclusion) and working with partners to save and change the lives of those WFP serves.

To learn more about WFP, visit our website: https://www.wfp.org and follow us on social media to keep up with our latest news: YouTube, LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, Twitter, TikTok.

WHY JOIN WFP?

  • WFP is a 2020 Nobel Peace Prize Laureate.
  • WFP offers a highly inclusive, diverse, and multicultural working environment.
  • WFP invests in the personal & professional development of its employees through a range of training, accreditation, coaching, mentorship, and other programs as well as through internal mobility opportunities.
  • A career path in WFP provides an exciting opportunity to work across the various country, regional and global offices around the world, and with passionate colleagues who work tirelessly to ensure that effective humanitarian assistance reaches millions of people across the globe.
  • We offer an attractive compensation package (please refer to the Terms and Conditions section of this vacancy announcement).
  • WFP encourages female candidates and people with disabilities to apply.

BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE OF THE ASSIGNMENT:

Job holders at this level demonstrate responsibility and initiative to respond independently to queries with only general guidance. There is a requirement to use judgment in dealing with unforeseen problems on a daily basis. Job holders have a level of expertise and knowledge to adapt and contribute to the development of systems and processes to continually improve the level of support provided. Job holders manage resources, and coach and coordinate with relevant security staff and with a team of travel support staff. These jobs may require reporting for duty on short notice. The incumbent reports to the Management Services Officer.

JOB PURPOSE:

To provide support and perform administration related duties and responsibilities. The incumbent will be the focal person for travel of WFP Country Office Nepal and coordinate security-related support services with the United Nations Department of Safety and Security (UNDSS) which include performing tasks related to the implementation of security measures. The position is equivalent to job category of Management Services Associate.

TERMS AND CONDITION

Position Title: Administrative Associate (Admin/Travel)

Contract Type: Special Service Agreement (SSA L6)
Level: SSA L6

Contract Duration: 6 months

Duty Station: Kathmandu, Nepal
Deadline of Application: 17.08.2026

WFP offers a competitive benefits package including salary plus CIGNA health insurance.

KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES/RESPONSIBILITIES (not all-inclusive, nor exhaustive):

1). Coordinate administrative and technical support within the Management Services portfolio to ensure efficient and high-quality service delivery.

2). Monitoring resources needs with designated areas of responsibilities (travel, security, facilities, assets, etc.) and assist in identifying new requirements to enhance operational efficiency and cost-effectiveness of services. Review and recommend improvements to relevant SOPs and procedures.

3). Collate and analyze relevant data and prepare and/or consolidate reports to contribute to decision-making and efficient management of resources.

4). Monitor and process actions related to procurement, finance and other relevant areas. Liaise with other functions and third-party contractors to enable efficient service delivery and seek better prices for travel as per WFP liability.

5). Process Trip documents for international air ticket issuance ensuring correct DSAs.

6). Utilize digital tools and technology applications to improve working practices and customer service and effectively adopt new technologies that are introduced at the workplace.

7). Participate in the preparation of inter-agency initiatives as part of UN Reform to achieve cost savings and enhancement of service quality.

8). Provide support to emergency preparedness and response by allocating resources, offering analytics, on related services.

9). Act as security focal person. Collate and analyze information from UNDSS and prepare and or consolidate reports to contribute to decision making and efficient management of resources.

10). Liaise with UNDSS in order to co-ordinate with local administration, security and law enforcement authorities, communities, UN/NGO security staff and other actors for safer programme delivery as required.

11). Support in reviewing security related information (e.g. security incidents and events, security support for daily activities, etc.). Update the security focal point at the Headquarters/Regional Security Advisor on security developments on a day-to-day basis.

12). Plan and co-ordinate staff activities during field missions and support in performing security assessments within the area of responsibility to support safe and effective programme delivery.

13). Assist the MS (Administration) Officer on security risk management matters and safety issues in compliance with the United Nations Security Management System (UNSMS) and support the implementation of risk management mitigation measures, including Minimum Operational Security Standards (MOSS) to ensure compliance.

14). Support the maintenance and management of security equipment and make recommendations to strengthen technology capacity in line with business requirements.

15). Monitor and ensure that all access control procedures are effective and stringently followed by all staff and visitors, to maintain a safe and secure environment.

16). Attend security meetings and coordinate with security focal points of other UN Agencies as and when required.

17). Train and guide the travel-related Business Support Assistants within other functional units in the area of work ensuring travel objectives are met in line with required standards.

18). Provide orientation to all staff to improve understanding of WFP travel regulations, policies, procedures, processes, standards, and systems. Review security training needs to develop measures to meet business requirements, liaise and coordinate with UNDSS for security training to staff.

19). Act as alternate in absence of Fleet Focal Point and perform duties as required.

Experience:

  • Sound understanding of general travel regulations, policies, procedures, processes, standards and systems.
  • General knowledge of procedures and systems used in security, asset and facility management.

Desired Knowledge & Skills:

  • Sound knowledge of travel related functions gained through relevant technical training or experience.
  • Ability to monitor and record travel related financial transactions.
  • Has experience in collating data and preparing reports pertaining to admin portfolio.
  • Has experience in coordinating the work of others and providing guidance and training.
  • Has experience working with teams across different functional areas.
  • Ability to manage emergency situations and remain calm.
  • Excellent communication skills to maintain frequent correspondence with both, internal staff and external authorities.
  • General knowledge and understanding of security administration, risk assessment and co-ordination with local authorities and local law enforcement agencies.
  • Attention to detail and constant vigilance in order to promptly detect any breach in security measures.

Languages:

Job Description

Introduction

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

Applications are welcome from internal and external candidates. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process. For the purpose of this vacancy, internal and internal-equivalent candidates are considered as first-tier candidates.

Organizational Context and Scope

Under the overall supervision of the Chief Migration Health Officer (CMHO) and direct supervision of the Senior Laboratory Technologist, the incumbent will be responsible for technical support to laboratory services with respect to Migration Health Assessments (HAP) and other programmes implemented by the IOM Migration Health Division in country Kathmandu, NEPAL.

Responsibilities

1. Perform laboratory procedures as assigned by the laboratory supervisor for pre-examination, examination, and post-examination activities through the use of the standard relevant equipment.

2. Contribute to the implementation of laboratory quality management systems under the guidance of the laboratory supervisor. Take on the focal point role for one or more quality system essentials (QSE) as requested by the laboratory supervisor.

3. Ensure standards and the quality of laboratory procedures by strictly following the Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).

4. Adhere to biosafety measures adopted in the laboratory, being responsible for the safety of oneself and others.

5. Organize and operate activities on assigned station for accurate, efficient and timely delivery of results.

6. Perform quality control and quality assurance activities for assigned stations and document results as required.

7. Facilitate laboratory equipment maintenance to ensure these are in good working order and operate equipment appropriately following SOPs.

8. Facilitate laboratory stock management and monitor that the equipment and consumables are sufficient for the anticipated work.

9. Alert the laboratory supervisor to any problems related to operations, including equipment, stock management and biosafety.

10. Facilitate maintenance of established systems of organized record keeping and information management for timely delivery of results, data collection, analysis and reporting for laboratory monitoring and facilitation of operational research.

11. Develop and/or update SOPs in coordination with the laboratory supervisor.

12. Participate in the improvement of the service system according to the adopted work plan in the laboratory.

13. Manage and meet client expectations by prioritizing interests and providing services with guiding principles of patients’ dignity, beneficence and non-maleficence in courteous manner.

14. Ensures compliance with IOM instruction INS 278 and undertakes all designated mandatory trainings.

15. Perform such other duties as may be assigned.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications and Experience

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree or Diploma from an accredited academic institution in Medical (Clinical) Laboratory Sciences, Microbiology or a related discipline in countries where the scope of responsibilities are fulfilled according to national regulations.
  • A valid license to practice is required.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

Experience

  • Three years for Bachelor’s degree holder and five years for diploma holders of relevant clinical laboratory experience in a busy institution, preferably in a laboratory;
  • Relevant technical knowledge and practices to personnel and laboratory operations;
  • Knowledge and experience in clinical laboratory techniques;
  • Knowledge of laboratory quality management systems;
  • Knowledge of the principles and practices laboratory biosafety;
  • Computer literate with understanding of accurate data collection and analysis for monitoring and continuous improvement of laboratory services and performances; and,
  • Good awareness of the laboratory role in health systems, optional use of resources for quality and efficient services delivery;
  • Proven laboratory expertise and/or advanced degree in laboratory specialization is an advantage.

Skills

  • Effectively applies and transfers relevant technical knowledge and practices to personnel and laboratory operations
  • Organizational skills;
  • Communication skills.

Languages

All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM’s official languages (English, French, Spanish).

For this position, fluency in English and Nepali language is required (oral and written).

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

Required Competencies

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

  • Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.

Managerial Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2, if with direct reports

The Organization:

Lutheran World Relief, which is part of Corus International, has been present in Nepal since 2011. Corus International is the parent of a family of world-class organizations working to deliver the holistic, lasting solutions needed to end extreme poverty once and for all. We are a global leader in international development, with 150 years of combined experience across our brands. Our nonprofit and for-profit subsidiaries include IMA World Health and its fundraising brand Corus World Health, Lutheran World Relief, CGA Technologies, Ground Up Investing, and Farmers Market Brands. In Nepal, Corus operates under Lutheran World Relief. Our more than 400 employees around the globe are experts in their fields and dedicated to helping the world’s most vulnerable people break the cycle of poverty and lead healthy lives.

At Corus we believe that good only grows stronger and we reflect that belief in our workplace culture. We value every employee’s specialized area of expertise and nurture professional growth. We promote an engaging and supportive work environment, where employees feel enabled and driven to innovate, learn and collaborate. And because our subsidiaries often function as partners, our employees have the opportunity to work across our enterprise family.

Job Brief:

Position Summary: This position will be an employee of Lutheran World Relief. The RISE Fund project strengthens disaster preparedness, governance, and resilience in Nepal’s most vulnerable provinces, Karnali and Sudurpaschim. The program runs across multiple sectors to reduce humanitarian risks and build inclusive disaster risk management systems.

The program has four interlinked components:

  • Emergency Preparedness & Coordination – establishing rapid response teams, provincial search and rescue units, and activating emergency operations centers.
  • Shelter & Relief Support – pre-positioning emergency supplies, constructing temporary shelters, and ensuring rapid deployment within 24-72 hours after disasters.
  • Health & WASH Services – training health workers, deploying mobile medical camps, distributing dignity kits, and restoring safe water and sanitation systems.
  • Protection & Logistics – providing mental health and psychosocial support, safeguarding vulnerable groups, and creating an emergency transportation fund for rapid deployment.

The project aims to work with the provincial government to enable them to target 13 priority districts and 116 municipalities, directly benefiting over 30,000 individuals and indirectly reaching more than 500,000 people.

FAO’s commitment to environmental sustainability is integral to our strategic objectives and operations.

The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) contributes to the achievement of the 2030 Agenda through FAO Strategic Framework by supporting the transformation to MORE efficient, inclusive, resilient and sustainable agrifood systems, for better production, better nutrition, a better environment, and a better life, leaving no one behind.

Organizational setting

FAO is a specialized agency of the UN that leads international efforts to defeat hunger. FAO’s goal is to achieve food security for all and ensure that people have regular access to enough high-quality food to lead active, healthy lives. With 195 Members (194 countries and the European Union), FAO works in over 130 countries worldwide.

The main aim of the FAO Country Offices, which are headed by FAO Representatives (FAORs), is to assist governments to develop policies, programmes and projects to achieve food security and to reduce hunger and malnutrition, to help develop the agricultural, fisheries and forestry sectors, and to use their environmental and natural resources in a sustainable manner.

Specific activities of the Country Offices include:

  •  Implementing FAO’s field projects and participating in the development of the Field Programme by identifying” and formulating new projects and liaising with local donor representatives.
  • Helping governments to prevent and assess the damage of disasters and assisting them in the reconstruction and rehabilitation of the agricultural sector.
  •  Carrying out public awareness activities and support important FAO campaigns such as the World Food Day (WFD).
  •  Providing assistance to technical and investment missions from FAO headquarters and from Regional or Subregional Offices to the country.
  •  Serving as a channel for FAO’s services to governments and other partners (donors, non-governmental organizations (NGOs), civil society organizations (CSOs), research institutions, etc.).
  • Keeping FAO informed of major social and economic developments in the country and monitoring the situation of the agriculture sector in the country.
  • Acting as FAO Representative to host governments and all partners involved in FAO activities.

Reporting Lines

The Young Professional Officer (Climate Change and Natural Resources Management) reports to the Assistant FAO Representative (Programme) and collaborates closely with the relevant Climate Change Project leads in close collaboration with other programme colleagues.

Technical Focus

The Young Professional Officer (Climate Change and Natural Resources Management) assists with the development and implementation of FAO programmes and activities related to climate change and natural resources management in Nepal. More specifically, he/she will assist the project leads to manage climate change adaptation, mitigation and resilience interventions within FAO Nepal’s agriculture, forestry and sustainable natural resource management sectors, aligning with government priorities and in line with the priorities set forth by FAO Nepal’s Country Programming Framework (CPF) (2023-2027).

Key Results

Research, technical analysis and project related services to support the delivery of assigned projects, products and services.

Key Functions

  • Analyses relevant technical social, economic, environmental, and technology information, data and/or statistics for input in various documents.
  •  Maintains records and updates databases and web pages.
  •  Provides technical support to various projects.
  •  Collaborates in the development of training tools and materials and the organization of workshops/seminars, etc.
  • Participates in the organization and follow-up of meetings, consultations and conferences, the production of required materials and the provision of information and assistance to partners.

Specific Functions

  • Assists in the coordination and implementation of ongoing (National, Regional and Global) climate change-related programmes and projects in the areas of agriculture, forestry, and natural resource management.
  •  Supports the preparation of concept notes and project proposals in the areas of climate change and natural resource management, as well as related resource mobilization efforts.
  •  Supports the programme leads in monitoring projects, including compiling inputs for revisions, tracking expenditures and resources, and flagging potential discrepancies against budget lines.
  • Assists in maintaining the completeness and quality of data and documentation in FAO’s corporate systems for assigned operational field projects and activities.
  • Participates and assists in supporting the development of partnerships with relevant organizations and stakeholders, including government agencies, UN agencies, NGOs, and the private sector.
  • Participates and assists in the organization of policy dialogues, workshops, and consultation meetings in coordination with the programme team and stakeholders.
  • Contributes to stakeholder engagement and awareness-raising activities, including preparation of communication and outreach materials; and
    Performs other related duties as required.

CANDIDATES WILL BE ASSESSED AGAINST THE FOLLOWING

Minimum Requirements

  •  Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in areas such as agriculture, climate change, environmental science, natural resource management or any other fields.
  •  One year of relevant experience in supporting including exposure to the implementation of climate change and natural resource management projects and programmes.
  •  Working knowledge of English (proficiency – Level C) and intermediate knowledge (intermediate proficiency – level B) of another FAO official language (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian or Spanish).

Competencies

  •  Results Focus
  • Teamwork

  • Knowledge Sharing and Continuous Improvement

Technical/Functional Skills

  • Extent and relevance of experience in related fields such as climate change, natural resource management, food and nutrition security, agricultural development and disaster risk reduction
  •  Extent and relevance of experience in the preparation, editing and revision of technical/scientific documents and in organizing meetings and workshops
  •  Extent and relevance of experience in supporting partnerships with UN agencies, NGOs as well as donors and government institutions and agencies
  •  Working knowledge of another FAO language would be an asset
  •  Work experience in more than one location or area of work, particularly in field positions, is desirable.

The Copywriter is responsible for bringing eSewa brand to life through impactful storytelling and compelling copy that inspires action and builds emotional connections with customers. The role goes beyond writing as it requires translating marketing strategies into meaningful narratives that seamlessly connect visuals with words, ensuring every communication reflects eSewa’s brand promise.

Working closely with designers, marketers, product teams, and business stakeholders, the Copywriter will create audience-centric communication that resonates across customer segments, occasions, and platforms.

Qualification and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Mass Communication, Journalism, English, Business Administration, or a related field.
  • 1–3 years of experience in copywriting, content writing, advertising, digital marketing, or brand communication.
  • Experience in fintech, banking, technology, consumer brands, or advertising agencies will be an added advantage.

Job Description

  • Develop compelling copy for integrated marketing campaigns, product launches, seasonal campaigns, and always-on brand communication.
  • Craft engaging content for social media, digital advertisements, app banners, landing pages, websites, blogs, emailers, SMS, push notifications (FCM), in-app communication, video scripts, press releases, and other marketing assets.
  • Partner closely with designers to ensure copy and visuals work together to tell a cohesive, emotionally engaging story rather than functioning as separate elements.

Background: The Adventist Development and Relief Agency (ADRA) is a global humanitarian organization with a mission to work with people in poverty and distress to create just and positive change. ADRA Nepal belongs to the worldwide ADRA network, comprised of more than 100 supporting and implementing country offices. Operating in Nepal since 1987, ADRA has been a trusted partner for 40+ years in health, livelihoods, education, and disaster risk management. It collaborates with all levels of government and civil society, focusing on Madhesh, Bagmati, Lumbini, Karnali, and Sudurpashchim Provinces, with presence in 150+ municipalities across 20 districts.

Required positions: The following four (4) positions are required for the delivery of Institutional Service for Quality Improvement in Emergency Obstetric and Newborn Care (EmONC) and Sick Newborn Care Units (SNCUs) in Lumbini Province. Periodic field visits for supervision and joint monitoring.

About the Organization

Kapilvastu Integrated Development Services (KIDS) is a non-governmental, non- profit, and non-political organization established on 31 August 2005 in Kapilvastu District, Nepal. The organization is duly registered with the District Administration Office and affiliated with the Social Welfare Council (SWC) since 20 March 2007.

KIDS was founded by committed community members with the vision of fostering a Healthy, inclusive and prosperous society with full of peace and equal justice. Since its establishment, the organization has worked to improve the quality of life of vulnerable and marginalized communities through inclusive, community-driven, and sustainable development interventions.

KIDS implements development and humanitarian programs across Lumbini Province in partnership with government agencies, national and international NGOs, UN agencies, donor organizations, and local communities. Its core thematic areas include Health, Nutrition, Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH), Food Security and Livelihoods, Climate Change Adaptation, Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR), Child Protection, Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI), Education, and Community Empowerment.

The organization is committed to maintaining the highest standards of good governance, transparency, accountability, safeguarding, financial stewardship, and compliance with the Government of Nepal’s legal and regulatory framework, donor requirements, and internationally recognized humanitarian and development principles. KIDS promotes integrity, ethical conduct, gender equality, inclusion, environmental responsibility, and a culture of continuous learning and organizational excellence in all aspects of its work.

The Junior Technical Assistant (Livestock/ veterinary) will provide field-level technical

Job Summary

support to livestock farmers and entrepreneurs under the SaBaS Project. The position will promote livestock farming practices and support enterprise development through regular technical guidance, training, monitoring, and coordination with local stakeholders. This
reflects the typical role of JTAs in Nepal’s livestock and livelihood projects.

Primary Responsibilities

Key Responsibilities

  •  Conduct regular field visits to monitor the health and condition of livestock and poultry.
  •  Provide basic veterinary first aid and technical support within the scope of VJTA responsibilities.
  •  Identify common signs and symptoms of livestock and poultry diseases and provide appropriate technical advice.
  •  Support disease prevention, control, and management activities.
  •  Assist in vaccination, deworming, parasite control, and other animal health campaigns as authorized.
  •  Maintain proper records of animal health services provided.
  •  Identify complicated or emergency cases and refer them to a qualified veterinarian or appropriate veterinary service provider.
  •  Provide technical advice to farmers on scientific livestock management practices.
  •  Promote improved cattle, buffalo and goat management practices.
  •  Support farmers in improving animal housing, sanitation, hygiene and biosecurity.
  •  Provide technical guidance on breeding, reproduction and general livestock management.
  •  Coordinate with livestock section on palika level or ward level.
  •  Coordinate with supervisor for taken proper guidelines and support.

Qualifications, Experience, Knowledge, and Skills

Qualifications and Experience

  •  Diploma/JTA/ TSLC in Livestock/ veterinary science from a recognized institution.
  •  2 years of relevant work experience in livestock, animal health, veterinary services, farmer mobilization, or community-based livestock programs.
  •  Good knowledge of livestock health, disease prevention, vaccination, deworming, animal nutrition, breeding, husbandry and basic veterinary practices.
  •  Field experience: Experience working directly with farmers, livestock groups and rural communities will be an advantage.

  •  Valid two-wheeler driving license with willingness to travel extensively within Kapilvastu is preferred.

Posiiton: Children’s Home Associate
Location: Surkhet, Karnali

“A world where every child is safe, educated, loved”- Kopila Valley Sewa Samaj is a non-profitable NGO registered in Surkhet, Nepal to provide support for children and families in our community. Our mission is to change the world by empowering Nepal’s children. KVSS programs include a residential children’s home, Kopila Valley School (KVS) for inclusive quality education, women’s empowerment, sustainability, health and wellness, and family development programs. We provide our students with free education, educational materials, health treatment and medicine, counseling, and a place to live. With our innovative future program, we strive to provide our children with career guidance, and scholarships for further studies. Our children’s home provides a safe, loving, and stable home for children in extreme cases of need, when all other options have been exhausted. We do this with our funding partner BlinkNow Foundation and in close ties with the local government and communities.

Position Summary-

The Staff working at KVSS should have patient and passionate about working with children will thrive as childcare. Should be enthusiastic about the growth and well-being of Children, sensitive to their needs, able to mix, relax and interact socially with children and be linked and respected by Children. The Children Home Associate at Children’s Home is responsible for the care, wellbeing, and upbringing of the children living within the KV Children’s Home. Your role is to provide basic parental, pastoral, and holistic care to provide the children with the brightest future possible. It is also your responsibility to manage and coordinate with all the other staff members working within the KV Children’s Home, and make sure that all caregiving roles are running as smoothly as possible.

The Employee will be required to perform the following duties and undertake the following responsibilities in a professional manner.

Job Description

The Main Responsibilities

  • Make sure that the children at KV Children’s Home are cared for and supported in the best way possible.
  • Support to manage caregivers and other support team members.
  • Assist in enrichment activities of the children.

Detailed Responsibilities

1.Make sure that the children at Kopila Valley Children’s Home are cared for and supported in the best possible way.

  • Create and update routines for the activities of children in Kopila Valley Children Home, and make sure that they are followed properly.
  • Lead daily gathering (sutsang) for children after dinner.
  • Manage activities that are designed to promote physical, mental, and social development of children.
  • Support children in their education- ensure that they study for an appropriate period regularly, and manage interactive activities and support children to learn, grow and feel proud.
  • Support children to make sure that they are done with all the chores that they are supposed to do before school
  • Performing regular check-in with the children in a one-to-one format in order to provide support and engage their needs.

2.Support to manage caregivers and other support team members.

  • Supervise the work of caregivers at the children’s home daily and provide continued feedback for any improvements required to improve services.
  • Coordinate with the admin team in regards to any necessary items for children.
  • Demonstrate discipline from personal behavior, initiate it for the team to demonstrate, and encourage it to flow from the team to the children.
  • Support caregivers to address any obstacles or challenges they may face.
  • Evaluate the performance of the home caregivers and support them in their professional development.
  • Coordinate with relevant team members to run all other children’s home functions smoothly.

3.Assist in Academic and non academic activities of the Children

  • Support children during their home works and study time.
  • Assist in non academic activities as planned by the Enrichment coordinator.
  • Prepare engagement activities independently during their free time with the support of caregivers.
  • Ensure that children’s study time tables are duly followed as per the time table.

Additional expectations

  • Take ownership of change and engage and encourage innovation.
  • Build positive working relationships and environment in the organization by bringing solutions to the discussion table.
  • Report to the manager on a weekly basis, and as needed in case of urgent activities.
  • Build and maintain a strong relationship with the children, staff and relevant stakeholders.
  • Attend weekly staff meetings and share operational updates.
  • Always maintain integrity and confidentiality.
  • The above list of responsibilities is not comprehensive, and candidates may be required to take on additional responsibilities, as determined by your supervisor.

Must Have

  • Education: +2 in Social science or any discipline.
  • Experience: At least 3 years of proven experience in a residential care or child protection field
  • Language: A good communicator, fluent in Nepali and basic in English
  • Skills and Abilities: Ability to manage, mentor and lead children, youth, their activities
  • Passionate about and cares for children and vulnerable population; initiator, and competent in managing caregivers, children and basic operations.
  • Works collaboratively and independently with the least supervision required.

Note: This is a residential and immersive role where the Children Home Associate needs to be hands on caregiving as well. Preferred Female.

Key Characteristics

  • You believe that we can change the world, in the blink of an eye
  • You believe in making decisions that put children first
  • You are self-motivated, organized, and approachable
  • You enjoy creating systems, keeping records, and increasing efficiency
  • You are always looking for new ways for our team to work smarter instead of harder
  • You are detail-oriented and conscientious. You make sure nothing slips through the cracks
  • You have a strong work ethic and a willingness to pick up new skills. You are comfortable multi-tasking
  • You are positive, patient, and a clear communicator who is comfortable working with both Kopila Valley staff in Nepal and the BlinkNow staff in the United States
  • You are an empathetic person, with a knack for putting out fires before they start and soothing conflicts brewing beneath the surface
  • You require little supervision and are flexible. You understand that you will be wearing many hats in this role, many of which are not explicitly included in this job description

Application Procedure

If you think this career opportunity will amplify your career growth, we encourage you to apply by clicking “Apply for this Job” and submit all required document. Only shortlisted candidates will be called for further screening process. No telephone inquiries will be entertained. We accept and screen applications on a rolling basis.

Position: Junior Technical Assistant (Agriculture)
Department: Program
Project/Program: Sabal Balika Sabal Samudaya (SaBaSS) Project
Reports to: Technical Coordinator (Enterprises Development)
Duty station: KIDS Central Office, Taulihawa, Kapilvastu, Lumbini Province
Employment Type: Full-time

About the Organization

Kapilvastu Integrated Development Services (KIDS) is a non-governmental, non- profit, and non-political organization established on 31 August 2005 in Kapilvastu District, Nepal. The organization is duly registered with the District Administration Office and affiliated with the Social Welfare Council (SWC) since 20 March 2007.

KIDS was founded by committed community members with the vision of fostering a Healthy, inclusive and prosperous society with full of peace and equal justice. Since its establishment, the organization has worked to improve the quality of life of vulnerable
and marginalized communities through inclusive, community-driven, and sustainable development interventions.

KIDS implements development and humanitarian programs across Lumbini Province in partnership with government agencies, national and international NGOs, UN agencies, donor organizations, and local communities. Its core thematic areas include Health, Nutrition, Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH), Food Security and Livelihoods, Climate Change Adaptation, Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR), Child Protection, Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI), Education, and Community Empowerment.

The organization is committed to maintaining the highest standards of good governance, transparency, accountability, safeguarding, financial stewardship, and compliance with the Government of Nepal’s legal and regulatory framework, donor requirements, and internationally recognized humanitarian and development principles. KIDS promotes integrity, ethical conduct, gender equality, inclusion, environmental responsibility, and a culture of continuous learning and organizational excellence in all aspects of its work.

The Junior Technical Assistant (Agriculture) will provide field-level technical support to

Job Summary

farmers, producer groups, and agri-entrepreneurs under the SaBaS Project. The position will promote climate-smart agriculture, improve productivity, strengthen market-oriented farming practices, farmer field school and support enterprise development through regular technical guidance, training, monitoring, and coordination with local stakeholders.

This reflects the typical role of JTAs in Nepal’s agriculture and livelihood projects.

Primary Responsibilities

Key Responsibilities

  •  Involvement in assessing livelihood opportunities through agriculture and assessing their feasibility.
  • Provide technical advisory services to farmers and producer groups on climate-resilient agriculture practices.
  • Conduct agriculture related training, farmer field school, demonstrations plots, develop model farms, field visits, and technical coaching.
  •  Support the distribution of agricultural inputs such as seeds, fertilizers, and tools to beneficiaries.
  •  Support the establishment and strengthening of farmer groups, cooperatives, and agri-enterprises.
  •  Conduct regular field visits to monitor crop performance and provide timely recommendations.
  •  Assist in implementing project activities related to enterprise development, value chains, and market linkages.
  •  Collect field data, maintain records, and prepare monthly progress reports.
  •  Monitor crop performance, identify production constraints, and recommend appropriate technical solutions.
  •  Coordinate with local governments, agriculture offices, cooperatives, and other stakeholders.
  •  Support in linking farmers to markets, input suppliers, and financial institutions.
  •  Ensure gender equality, social inclusion (GESI), and environmental sustainability are integrated into project activities.
  •  Perform other project-related duties assigned by the supervisor.
  •  Prepare periodic reports and share key findings with the Livelihood Coordinator.
  •  Represent the organization in community and palika level in agriculture related meetings and events.

Qualifications, Experience, Knowledge, and Skills

Qualifications and Experience

  • Diploma/TSLC /JTA in Agriculture (Plant Science) from a recognized institution.
  • At least 2 years of experience in agriculture extension, community mobilization, or livelihood projects.
  •  Good knowledge of vegetable production, integrated pest management (IPM), climate-smart agriculture, and farmer training.
  •  Strong communication and facilitation skills in Nepali; knowledge of local languages is an advantage.
  •  Valid two-wheeler driving license with willingness to travel extensively within Kapilvastu is preferred.

Application Instructions:

Interested candidates are requested to apply via email with a recently updated CV and cover letter by 12th August 2026 to: procurement.kids@gmail.com

More information: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/17ATa3uulyEtqbujjdzn6AQswmkZC2Vo5?usp=sharing

  • Only short-listed candidates will be contacted for further selection process
  • Telephone enquiry will not be entertained

Position: Procurement & Logistics Officer
Department: Administration Depart
Project/Program: Sabal Balika Sabal Samudaya (SaBaSS) – Project
Reports to: Senior Administrative & Finance Officer / Executive Director
Duty station: KIDS Central Office, Taulihawa, Kapilvastu, Lumbini Province
Employment Type: Full-time

About the Organization

Kapilvastu Integrated Development Services (KIDS) is a non-governmental, non- profit, and non-political organization established on 31 August 2005 in Kapilvastu District, Nepal. The organization is duly registered with the District Administration
Office and affiliated with the Social Welfare Council (SWC) since 20 March 2007.

KIDS was founded by committed community members with the vision of fostering an equitable, healthy, resilient, and self-reliant society. Since its establishment, the organization has worked to improve the quality of life of vulnerable and marginalized
communities through inclusive, community-driven, and sustainable development interventions.

KIDS implement development and humanitarian programs across Lumbini Province in partnership with government agencies, national and international NGOs, UN agencies, donor organizations, and local communities. Its core thematic areas include Health,
Nutrition, Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH), Food Security and Livelihoods, Climate Change Adaptation, Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR), Child Protection, Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI), Education, and Community Empowerment.

The organization is committed to maintaining the highest standards of good governance, transparency, accountability, safeguarding, financial stewardship, and compliance with the Government of Nepal’s legal and regulatory framework, donor requirements, and internationally recognized humanitarian and development principles. KIDS promote integrity, ethical conduct, gender equality, inclusion, environmental responsibility, and a culture of continuous learning and organizational excellence in all aspects of its work.

Job Summary

The Procurement & Logistics Officer is responsible for supporting the efficient planning, implementation, and monitoring of procurement, logistics, inventory, asset management, and fleet operations for organizational and project activities. The position
ensures that all procurement and logistics processes are conducted in compliance with the policies and procedures of Kapilvastu Integrated Development Services (KIDS), donor requirements, and the applicable laws and regulations of the Government of Nepal.

The Procurement & Logistics Officer coordinates the procurement of goods, works, and services through transparent, competitive, and value-for-money processes. The position is responsible for maintaining procurement documentation, managing supplier relationships, coordinating logistics arrangements, monitoring inventory and fixed assets, and ensuringthe timely delivery of supplies to support effective project implementation.

Working under the direct supervision of the Administration & Finance Manager/Senior Administration & Finance Officer (or designated supervisor), the Procurement & Logistics Officer collaborates closely with programme, finance,
administration, and field teams to ensure that procurement and logistics services are responsive to operational needs and donor compliance requirements. The position is expected to maintain high standards of integrity, accountability, confidentiality, and professionalism while contributing to efficient resource management, operational excellence, and the achievement of organizational objectives.

Primary Responsibilities

A. Procurement Management

  • Implement procurement activities in accordance with the organization’s Procurement Policy, donor regulations, and the applicable laws and regulations of the Government of Nepal.
  • Prepare and update procurement plans in coordination with project and support teams.
  • Receive, review, and process approved procurement requests ensuring completeness and budget availability.
  • Obtain quotations, conduct market surveys, and prepare comparative bid analysis to ensure competitive and value-for-money procurement.
  • Prepare Requests for Quotation (RFQs), purchase orders, purchase agreements, and other procurement documentation.
  • Coordinate bid opening, quotation evaluation, supplier selection, and procurement committee meetings as required.
  • Ensure procurement processes are transparent, fair, and properly documented.
  • Follow up with suppliers to ensure timely delivery of goods and services according to agreed specifications and delivery schedules.
  • Maintain procurement records and filing systems in both hard-copy and electronic formats.
  • Assist in preparing procurement reports and procurement status updates.

Logistics Management

  •  Coordinate the transportation, delivery, receipt, and distribution of project materials, equipment, and
    supplies.
  • Arrange logistics for meetings, workshops, training programs, field visits, and project events.
  • Ensure timely delivery of procurement items to project sites and end users.
  • Coordinate transportation arrangements for staff, consultants, visitors, and project activities as required.
  • Monitor delivery schedules and resolve logistics issues to minimize delays.

C. Inventory and Asset Management

  •  Maintain updated inventory records for office supplies, equipment, and project assets.
  •  Receive, inspect, record, and issue materials in accordance with organizational procedures.
  •  Conduct periodic physical stock counts and reconcile inventory records.
  •  Maintain an updated fixed asset register and ensure all assets are properly tagged.
  •  Report damaged, obsolete, or missing assets to the supervisor and support disposal processes in accordance with organizational policies.
  •  Ensure safe storage and proper handling of inventory and organizational assets.

D. Fleet and Office Support

  •  Maintain vehicle logbooks and monitor vehicle utilization, fuel consumption, servicing, insurance, and registration.
  •  Coordinate routine maintenance and repairs of vehicles and office equipment.
  •  Monitor office supplies and initiate procurement requests to maintain adequate stock levels.
  •  Support office administration by coordinating courier services, mail, office maintenance, and utility services when required.

E. Vendor and Contract Management

  •  Maintain an updated database of approved suppliers, contractors, and service providers.
  •  Assist in evaluating supplier performance and maintaining supplier records.
  • Monitor supplier deliveries and contract performance to ensure compliance with agreed terms and conditions.
  •  Coordinate with vendors to resolve delivery, quality, or service-related issues.

F. Compliance, Documentation, and Reporting

  •  Ensure procurement and logistics activities comply with organizational policies, donor requirements, and Government of Nepal regulations.
  •  Maintain complete procurement, logistics, inventory, and asset documentation for audit and donor review.
  •  Support internal audits, external audits, and donor monitoring visits by providing required documentation.
  •  Prepare monthly procurement, logistics, and inventory reports for management.
  •  Ensure proper filing and record retention in accordance with organizational and donor requirements.

G. Coordination and Communication

  •  Coordinate closely with Finance, Administration, and Program teams to ensure timely procurement and logistical support for project implementation.
  •  Liaise with suppliers, transport providers, government offices, and service providers regarding procurement and logistics matters.
  •  Participate in procurement committee meetings and provide administrative support as assigned.
  •  Communicate procurement progress and delivery status to relevant staff on a regular basis.

H. Safeguarding, Ethics, and Organizational Compliance

  • Comply with the organization’s Code of Conduct, Procurement Policy, Safeguarding Policy, Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) Policy, Anti-Fraud and Anti-Corruption Policy, and other
    organizational policies.
  • Promote transparency, accountability, fairness, confidentiality, and value for money in all procurement and logistics activities.
  • Ensure all work is carried out with integrity and in accordance with donor requirements and organizational standards.
  •  Maintain confidentiality of procurement information and supplier documentation.
  •  Contribute to a safe, respectful, inclusive, and collaborative working environment.
  •  Perform any other procurement, logistics, or administrative duties assigned by the Supervisor, Project Coordinator, or Executive Director that are consistent with the nature of the position.

Qualifications, Experience, Knowledge, and Skills

Education

  •  Bachelor’s degree in business administration/ management from a recognized university.

Professional Experience

  • Minimum 2 years of relevant professional experience in procurement, logistics, administration, or supply chain management, preferably in NGOs, INGOs, or donor-funded projects.
  •  Experience in implementing procurement processes, logistics coordination, inventory management, and vendor management.
  •  Experience in preparing procurement documentation, maintaining procurement records, and supporting procurement committee processes.
  •  Experience in coordinating transportation, delivery of goods, and warehouse or inventory management.
  •  Familiarity with donor-funded project procurement procedures is desirable.

Knowledge

  •  Good knowledge of procurement principles, logistics operations, inventory control, and asset management.
  •  Understanding of procurement policies, competitive bidding procedures, and value-for-money principles.
  •  Familiarity with the procurement requirements of donor-funded projects and the applicable laws and regulations of the Government of Nepal.
  •  Basic knowledge of contract management, supplier relationship management, and procurement documentation.
  •  Understanding of workplace health and safety, safeguarding, and ethical procurement practices.

Technical Skills

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Word, Excel, and Outlook.
  •  Ability to maintain procurement tracking sheets, inventory records, and asset registers.
  •  Experience using inventory management systems, procurement software, or ERP systems will be an advantage.
  •  Good record-keeping, filing, and documentation skills.
  •  Ability to prepare procurement reports and maintain accurate procurement and logistics records.

Core Competencies

  •  Procurement and Logistics Coordination
  •  Inventory and Asset Management
  •  Planning and Organizational Skills
  •  Attention to Detail
  •  Time Management and Ability to Meet Deadlines
  •  Problem Solving and Decision Making
  •  Communication and Interpersonal Skills
  •  Teamwork and Collaboration
  •  Integrity, Accountability, and Professional Ethics
  •  Adaptability and Willingness to Learn

Language Requirements

  •  Good written and verbal communication skills in English and Nepali.
  •  Ability to prepare procurement correspondence, reports, and official documentation in English.

Personal Attributes

  •  Honest, reliable, and committed to maintaining confidentiality.
  •  Strong organizational skills with attention to accuracy and detail.
  •  Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a multidisciplinary team.
  •  Ability to manage multiple tasks and work under pressure to meet deadlines.
  •  Commitment to transparency, accountability, safeguarding, and the values and mission of Kapilvastu Integrated Development Services (KIDS).

Application Instructions:

Interested candidates are requested to apply via email with a recently updated CV and cover letter by 12th August 2026 to: procurement.kids@gmail.com

  • Only short-listed candidates will be contacted for further selection process
  • Telephone enquiry will not be entertained

Its core thematic areas include Health, Nutrition, Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH), Food Security and Livelihoods, Climate Change Adaptation, Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR), Child

KIDS promote integrity, ethical conduct, gender equality, inclusion, environmental responsibility, and a culture of continuous learning and organizational excellence in all aspects of its work.

Job Summary

The Monitoring, Evaluation, Research and Learning (MERL) Officer has a role in planning organizing carrying out and making better the Monitoring, Evaluation, Research and Learning (MERL) system for the Sabal Balika Sabal Samudaya (SaBaSS) and
Sponsorship Communication Project. This role makes sure that program data is collected, checked, studied understood and sharedin timely manner with the relevant stakeholdesr. The position helps in making timely informed decisions which allows the program to act according to program information/dataway,The position also work according to the donor requirements- and learn more as an organization.

The MERL Officer is in charge of creating and using monitoring plans, tracking numbers, making sure that the collected data is efficient, effective and correct. With the use of digital tools the position is responsible in checking the data quality through regular checks, data triangulation and source data verification. The role maintains the data base in order which supports in writing relevant reports and internal and external sharing documents with special emphasis on knowledge sharing so that the program can be more effective and impactful.

This position works under the guidance of the Project Coordinator. Works closely with the teams that handle the program, safety, sponsorships and technical issues. The MERL Officer makes sure that everything follows the rules of KIDS, the MERL standards of
Plan International Nepal what the donors want and the rules from the Government of Nepal. The role also helps with being responsible by making community feedback systems making sure data is honest keeping private data safe and helping the people working on the project and the partners learn more about the tools, ways and standards for MERL. By checking all the time making sure the information is correct and learning from the work the MERL Officer helps reach the goals of the project make the program better.
Help children, young people, families and communities, in the project areas.

Primary Responsibilities

A. Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning

  •  Develop periodic MERL work plans that match project objectives and donor requirements.
  • Maintain and regularly update project monitoring tools, indicator tracking systems and reporting mechanisms.
  • Regular monitoring of project outputs, outcomes and impact indicators and informing the program on timely basis.
  • Against the set targets check the performance of the project and suggest changes to make the program better and more effective.

The organization is duly registered with the District Administration Office and affiliated with the Social Welfare Council (SWC) since 20 March 2007.
KIDS was founded by committed community members with the vision of fostering a Healthy, inclusive and prosperous society with full of peace and equal justice. Since its establishment, the organization has worked to improve the quality of life of vulnerable and marginalized communities through inclusive, community-driven, and sustainable development interventions.
KIDS implements development and humanitarian programs across Lumbini Province in partnership with government agencies, national and international NGOs, UN agencies, donor organizations, and local communities. The organization is committed to maintaining the highest standards of good governance, transparency, accountability, safeguarding, financial stewardship, and compliance with the Government of Nepal’s legal and regulatory framework, donor requirements, and internationally recognized humanitarian and development principles.
